definition_zh: 鲨鱼；骗子；放高利贷的人；专家；勒索；欺诈
definition_en: a large sea fish with a pointed snout and sharp teeth, or, by extension, a person who cheats others and a keen expert in some field
core_image: 背鳍像一把尖刀划破海面，水下是张开的锯齿大嘴
scene: 浅滩上有人大声提醒游客别游得太远，因为水里出现了背鳍。On the crowded beach a lifeguard pointed at a dark fin and warned the swimmers that a shark was close to the shore.
sceneCN: 这里 shark 是「鲨鱼」（第 1 个义项：海中具有尖吻和利齿的大型鱼类）；句意：在拥挤的海滩上，救生员指着一条黑色的背鳍，警告游泳者附近有一条鲨鱼。

pos.zh: 鲨鱼；骗子；放高利贷的人；行家
勒索；诈骗；坑骗

collocations.zh: 牌技高手；以牌局行骗的人

derivatives.zh: shark 加动名词后缀 -ing，作名词时指「鲨鱼捕捞；猎鲨」，口语中也可指「诈骗行为」
shark 与 skin（皮）合成的名词，指「鲨鱼皮；鲨皮布」，一种曾用于泳衣的粗糙织物
shark 加形容词后缀 -like（像……的），义为「鲨鱼般的；冷酷贪婪的」

senses.title: A large predatory sea fish
senses.definition: a large fish of the open sea that has a pointed snout, several rows of sharp teeth, and a tough skin
senses.definitionCN: 生活在开阔海域的大型鱼类，吻部尖、牙齿成排且锋利，皮肤坚韧
senses.example: The diver kept a safe distance from the shark.
senses.exampleCN: 潜水员与那条鲨鱼保持着安全距离。
senses.why: The word first named the fish itself, whose fin slicing through the surface became the picture of a swift ocean hunter.
senses.whyCN: 这个词原本就指这种鱼；它露出水面的背鳍，成了海中迅捷猎手的画面。

senses.title: A person who cheats others
senses.definition: a person who gains money by tricking or cheating other people
senses.definitionCN: 靠欺骗或耍花招骗取他人钱财的人
senses.example: That ticket shark sells fake passes outside the stadium.
senses.exampleCN: 那个倒票骗子在体育场外卖假通行证。
senses.why: Losing money to a cheat feels like being bitten, so the fish of the sharp teeth turned into a name for a swindler.
senses.whyCN: 被骗子掏走钱就像被咬掉一块，于是利齿的鱼被借来指行骗的人。

senses.title: A money lender at illegal rates
senses.definition: someone who lends money at very high, often illegal, rates of interest
senses.definitionCN: 以极高且常属非法的利息放款的人
senses.example: He borrowed from a loan shark and could not repay the interest.
senses.exampleCN: 他向高利贷者借了钱，结果连利息都还不上。
senses.why: An unregulated lender circles people in debt like a fish circling its prey, so the fixed phrase loan shark was born.
senses.whyCN: 无牌照的放款人像鱼围着猎物打转一样缠住负债者，loan shark 这一固定说法由此而来。

senses.title: An expert at a game or skill
senses.definition: a person who is extremely skillful at a game, especially one played for money
senses.definitionCN: 在某项游戏或技艺上极为娴熟的人，尤指赌局中的老手
senses.example: She is a pool shark who never loses a night game.
senses.exampleCN: 她是个台球高手，夜里打球从没输过。
senses.why: A player who picks off opponents one by one is prowling like a predator, so the fish name praises ruthless skill.
senses.whyCN: 能把对手逐个击倒的玩家像捕食者一样游弋，于是鱼的称呼也用来夸这种狠而精湛的本事。

senses.title: To swindle someone
senses.definition: to get money or goods from someone by deceit, often in a casual or slangy way
senses.definitionCN: 以欺骗手段从别人那里得到钱财或物品，多为随意或俚俗用法
senses.example: Two men had sharked the tourists out of their savings.
senses.exampleCN: 两个男人骗走了游客们的积蓄。
senses.why: Once the noun meant a cheat, English could turn it into a verb meaning to act like one.
senses.whyCN: 名词既然已能指骗子，英语就能把它动词化，表示做出骗子那样的行为。

senses.title: A difficult trained animal role
senses.definition: in animal training and travelling shows, the demanding role of an animal made to perform before a crowd, as in the old phrase doing the shark
senses.definitionCN: 在驯兽与巡回演出中，让动物在人群前表演的艰难活计，沿用一句老话 the shark
senses.example: Showing off a seal doing the shark was the finale of the show.
senses.exampleCN: 让一只海豹表演最难的把式，是这场演出的压轴节目。
senses.why: A show that trained a sea predator raised the small local word for that animal to a general name for a hard role.
senses.whyCN: 有驯兽表演把海中猛兽训练出来，这个当地小词就被抬高，成为指艰难行当的泛称。

senses.title: Shark meat or shark fin as food
senses.definition: the flesh of a shark used as food, or its fin prepared for soup
senses.definitionCN: 作为食物的鲨鱼肉，或用来做汤的鱼翅
senses.example: Some restaurants now refuse to serve shark because the practice is controversial.
senses.exampleCN: 如今有些餐厅因这种做法备受争议而拒绝供应鲨鱼。
senses.why: Trade and menus name the catch after the animal, so the whole fish, especially the valuable fin, became a food word.
senses.whyCN: 买卖与菜单都拿动物本身来称呼渔获，于是整条鱼尤其是值钱的鱼鳍成了食材名。

intro.en: Shark is a word of uncertain origin that appears in English in the sixteenth century; most reference works trace it to the seafarers of the Caribbean and their word for a large fish, but no etymology is settled.
intro.cn: shark 来源不确定，十六世纪才出现在英语中；多数辞书认为它来自加勒比地区航海者对某种大鱼的称呼，但词源尚无定论。

items.en: Sailors in the Caribbean are thought to have used a word for a big sea fish; some sources give the reconstructed form xoc from a Mayan language, which many linguists treat with caution.
items.cn: 一般认为加勒比地区的水手用某个词指一种大型海鱼；有资料给出玛雅语系的重构形式 xoc，但不少语言学者对此持谨慎态度。

items.en: Shark enters written English in the 1560s, first as the name of the fish seen on Atlantic voyages.
items.cn: shark 在一五六〇年代进入书面英语，最初指大西洋航行中见到的这种鱼。

items.en: The word is soon used for a person who lives by fraud, and the verb to shark, meaning to swindle or to live by one wits, appears at the end of the century.
items.cn: 这个词很快被用来指靠骗局谋生的人，世纪末又出现动词 shark，意为行骗或靠小聪明糊口。

items.en: Card playing and gambling give the sense of a skilled player, recorded in the nineteenth century as card shark and pool shark.
items.cn: 牌局与赌博带来「高手」这一义，十九世纪记录为 card shark 与 pool shark。

items.en: Loan shark for an illegal money lender is fixed in the twentieth century, and shark also names the meat and the fin used in cooking.
items.cn: 二十世纪定下了 loan shark 指非法放高利贷者；shark 又指作为食材的鲨鱼肉与鱼翅。

note.en: Shark has a small word family of its own, and in meaning it sits near other sea predators and near words for swindlers and unscrupulous lenders.
note.cn: shark 自成一个很小的词族，意义上与其它海洋掠食者相邻，也与骗子和无良放贷者的说法相邻。

entries.definition: shark skin, or a smooth fabric woven to look like it
entries.definitionCN: 鲨鱼皮，也指仿鲨鱼皮纹理的光滑织物，由 shark 与 skin 合成

entries.definition: resembling a shark, especially in being greedy or ruthless
entries.definitionCN: 像鲨鱼一样的，尤指贪婪冷酷，由 shark 加 -like 构成

entries.definition: the catching of sharks, or a swindle as a casual noun
entries.definitionCN: 捕鲨；口语中也指骗人的勾当，由 shark 加 -ing 构成

entries.definition: a person who cheats others out of money
entries.definitionCN: 诈骗钱财的人，与 shark 的第 2 个义项相近

entries.definition: a person who lends money at excessive interest
entries.definitionCN: 放高利贷者，是 loan shark 的正式同义词

entries.definition: a long, fierce fish of warm seas with sharp teeth
entries.definitionCN: 一种体长而凶猛的热带海鱼，牙齿锋利，常与鲨鱼一起被视为海中掠食者

normalIntro.en: Shark keeps the shape of a short sea word: one syllable, a sharp fin, and a family of compounds such as loan shark and card shark.
normalIntro.cn: shark 是个短促的海味词：一个音节，像一把尖鳍，又串出 loan shark 与 card shark 这样的合成说法。

normal.en: Loan shark is the fixed phrase for an illegal lender.
normal.cn: loan shark 是固定说法，指非法的放高利贷者。

normal.en: Card shark means a skilled or dishonest card player.
normal.cn: card shark 指牌技高超或出老千的牌手。

normal.en: Sharkskin is the rough skin of this fish and also a smooth fabric.
normal.cn: sharkskin 既是这种鱼粗糙的皮，也指一种光滑织物。

normal.en: Shark fin soup is a well-known dish; the uncountable shark alone can name the meat or the fin.
normal.cn: shark fin soup 是著名的一道汤；不加复数的 shark 本身就能指肉或鱼鳍。

normal.en: Compare whale and dolphin: both are warm-blooded air breathers, while the fish called shark breathes through gills.
normal.cn: 对比 whale 与 dolphin：它们都是温血、要用肺呼吸的动物，而 shark 是依靠鳃呼吸的鱼。

abstract.en: Picture the fin first, then the rows of teeth beneath the calm surface.
abstract.cn: 先看见背鳍，再想到平静水面下成排的牙齿。

abstract.en: Picture a crowd parting on the beach as the siren sounds.
abstract.cn: 想象警报响起，沙滩上的人群纷纷散开。

abstract.en: Picture a smooth grey shape sliding past the boat without a sound.
abstract.cn: 想象一个光滑的灰色身影无声地从船边滑过。

examples.en: Great white sharks can grow to more than five metres.
examples.cn: 大白鲨可以长到五米以上。

examples.en: Several beaches were closed after a shark attack.
examples.cn: 发生鲨鱼袭击事件后，几处海滩被关闭。

examples.en: The city has new rules to stop loan sharks from charging unfair interest.
examples.cn: 该市出台了新规定，禁止放高利贷者收取不合理的利息。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「傻克」——傻乎乎的人遇上鲨鱼只会被一口吃掉，所以 shark 是鲨鱼；谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: shark 来源不确定。一般认为十六世纪加勒比航海者用某个词指大鱼，英语在一五六〇年代借入，写作 sharke 或 shark；有资料提出玛雅语系的重构形式 xoc，但未成定论。

sensesIntro.en: Shark starts as the name of a predatory fish, then travels by metaphor to swindlers and greedy lenders, by praise to skilled players, and by trade to food.
sensesIntro.cn: shark 起于一种掠食鱼类之名，随后借比喻指骗子和贪婪的放贷者，借褒义指技艺高超的玩家，又借买卖指食材。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sharp fin cutting the surface while rows of teeth wait below.
core.cn: 核心意象：尖利的背鳍划破水面，水面下成排的牙齿正等着。

branches.en: The fish itself is the literal sense that everything else grows from.
branches.cn: 指这种鱼本身，是其它义项生长的字面根基。

branches.en: The bite turns into cheating and into lending money at cruel rates.
branches.cn: 被咬一口的痛感，转为行骗，也转为以苛刻利息放款。

branches.en: Prowling like a predator is praised as expert skill at a game.
branches.cn: 像捕食者般游弋，被用来称许游戏中的高手。

branches.en: The noun of the swindler becomes the verb of swindling.
branches.cn: 骗子的名词化为行骗的动词。

branches.en: Show business and the kitchen borrow the name for a hard role and for food.
branches.cn: 演出与厨房分别借它的名字指难上台的行当和食材。

intro.en: Shark is a single free morpheme with no productive affix of its own; the English family grows by compounding with skin and like, and by adding the noun and adjectival endings -ing and -like.
intro.cn: shark 是单独的自由语素，本身没有能产词缀；英语词族靠与 skin、like 合成，以及加 -ing、-like 这类名词与形容词词尾来扩展。

latinIntro.en: Shark has no accepted Latin ancestor; the fish known in Latin as squalus is unrelated in form, and the zoological name requiem for one shark family is likewise a later label.
latinIntro.cn: shark 没有公认的拉丁语祖源；拉丁语把这种鱼写作 squalus，形式上与它无关，而一类鲨鱼的动物学名 requiem 同样是后世才起的标签。

items.example: The base noun names the animal.
items.exampleCN: 这一基础名词指这种动物。

items.example: Sharks circled the boat.
items.exampleCN: 几条鲨鱼围着船打转。

items.example: Loan shark pairs shark with the money it takes.
items.exampleCN: loan shark 把 shark 与它吞下的钱配在一起。

items.meaning: a skilled or dishonest card player
items.meaningCN: 牌技高超或出老千的牌手
items.example: Card shark borrows the predator for skill.
items.exampleCN: card shark 借掠食者来夸本事。

items.meaning: shark skin or a rough fabric
items.example: Sharkskin joins shark and skin.
items.exampleCN: sharkskin 由 shark 与 skin 合成。

items.example: Sharklike describes a cold, greedy manner.
items.exampleCN: sharklike 形容冷酷贪婪的做派。

items.example: A sharklike smile made the offer feel unsafe.
items.exampleCN: 一个鲨鱼般的笑容让这份报价显得不可靠。

items.meaning: activity or the state of doing
items.meaningCN: 表示活动或正在进行的词尾
items.example: Sharking can name the catching of sharks.
items.exampleCN: sharking 可以指捕鲨。

items.example: Sharking also carries the cheating sense in speech.
items.exampleCN: 口语里 sharking 也带诈骗的意思。

items.example: Shark fin keeps shark as a modifier.
items.exampleCN: shark fin 里的 shark 作修饰语。

latinEntries.meaning: a kind of sea fish, often a shark
latinEntries.example: Latin squalus is not the source of shark.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 squalus 不是 shark 的来源。

definition_zh: 削尖；磨快；使敏锐；加剧；提高；变清晰
definition_en: to make something pointed or with a finer edge, and by extension to make a skill, a feeling, or a picture keener or clearer
core_image: 刀刃在磨石上来回推拉，灰色的铁屑一点点渗出来
scene: 做木工之前，老人总要在院子里把工具磨一磨，因为钝了就没法刻出细线。Before carving the chair leg, the old carpenter stopped to sharpen his chisel on a wet stone.
sceneCN: 这里 sharpen 是「磨快」（第 1 个义项：使刀刃或工具重新锋利）；句意：在雕刻椅子腿之前，老木匠停下来用湿磨石把凿子磨快。

pos.zh: 削尖；磨快；使敏锐；提高

derivatives.zh: 由 sharpen 加施事后缀 -er 构成的名词，指「磨具、削笔刀」
sharpen 去掉动词后缀 -en 所得的形容词，义为「锋利的；敏锐的；急剧的」
由现在分词转化的名词，指「磨快；加强」这一过程

senses.title: To give something a sharp edge
senses.definition: to make a blade or tool sharp again by grinding or filing it
senses.definitionCN: 通过研磨或锉削让刀刃、工具重新变得锋利
senses.example: He sharpened the knife before cutting the bread.
senses.exampleCN: 切面包之前他先把刀磨快了。
senses.why: The verb is sharp plus the ending -en that means to make, so sharpen is literally to make sharp.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词由表示「使……变得」的词尾 -en 加在形容词 sharp 后面构成，字面意思就是「使变锋利」。

senses.title: To give a pointed tip
senses.definition: to make the end of something pointed, especially a pencil or a stick
senses.definitionCN: 把某物的末端弄尖，尤指铅笔或木棍
senses.example: She sharpened her pencil and began to draw.
senses.exampleCN: 她把铅笔削尖，开始画画。
senses.why: A point is the smallest form of a sharp edge, so making anything pointed uses the same verb.
senses.whyCN: 尖端是锋利最浓缩的形态，于是把任何东西弄出尖头都用同一个动词。

senses.title: To make a skill keener
senses.definition: to improve a skill, the senses, or the mind so that it works more effectively
senses.definitionCN: 改进技能、感官或头脑，使其运作得更好
senses.example: Daily practice sharpened her ear for wrong notes.
senses.exampleCN: 每天练习让她更能听出音准上的毛病。
senses.why: A dull mind cuts poorly and a keen one cuts well, so training was pictured as grinding an edge.
senses.whyCN: 迟钝的头脑像钝刀切不动，敏锐的头脑像利刃，于是训练被比作在磨刀。

senses.title: To make a feeling more intense
senses.definition: to make an emotion, a difference, or a conflict stronger or more extreme
senses.definitionCN: 使情绪、差异或冲突变得更强烈或更极端
senses.example: The delay sharpened public anger.
senses.exampleCN: 拖延让公众的怒气更强烈了。
senses.why: If an edge gets sharper the cut gets deeper, so stronger feelings are described as a sharper pain or sharper desire.
senses.whyCN: 刀刃越锋利，划下去就越深，于是更强的情绪被形容为更尖锐的痛或更浓的渴望。

senses.title: To make something clearer
senses.definition: to make an image, an outline, or an argument easier to see or understand
senses.definitionCN: 让图像、轮廓或论证更容易看见或理解
senses.example: The new lens sharpened the details in the photo.
senses.exampleCN: 新镜头让照片里的细节清楚多了。
senses.why: A blurred edge becomes distinct once it is sharp, so sharpen means to make the border of an image crisp.
senses.whyCN: 模糊的边界一旦变「锐」就清楚了，所以 sharpen 表示把影像的边缘变得清晰锐利。

senses.title: For a price or situation to move sharply
senses.definition: used of prices, trade, or a mood, to become suddenly and steeply higher or more anxious
senses.definitionCN: 用于价格、交易或气氛，表示突然大幅上升或变得更加紧张
senses.example: Fuel prices sharpened after the storm closed the port.
senses.exampleCN: 暴风关闭港口后，燃料价格急剧上涨。
senses.why: The adjective sharp already describes a steep rise, so the verb lends its edge to lines on a price chart that rise like a blade.
senses.whyCN: 形容词 sharp 本来就形容陡然的上升，动词便把「锐」借给走势图上像刀刃一样翘起的曲线。

intro.en: Sharpen is formed in English from the adjective sharp with the verb ending -en; sharp goes back to Old English scearp and ultimately to a Germanic base meaning cutting.
intro.cn: sharpen 在英语中由形容词 sharp 加动词词尾 -en 构成；sharp 上溯古英语 scearp，再远源于日耳曼语中表示切割的语根。

items.en: A Germanic base meaning to cut or to scratch underlies the family, and the word is recorded across the North Sea languages.
items.cn: 日耳曼语中表示切割、刮擦的语根支撑着这个词族，该词在北海周围的多种语言中都有记录。

items.en: Old English scearp means cutting, keen, or severe, applied to blades and to painful things.
items.cn: 古英语 scearp 意为锐利的、锋利的、严厉的，既用于刀刃，也用于令人痛的事物。

items.en: Middle English sharp keeps both the physical edge and the keen sense applied to mind, sound, and price.
items.cn: 中古英语 sharp 兼指物理上的锋刃，以及用于头脑、声音、价格的敏锐之意。

items.en: English adds the ending -en, as in widen and deepen, so that sharpen means to make sharp and is first recorded in the fifteenth century.
items.cn: 英语加上了与 widen、deepen 相同的词尾 -en，使 sharpen 意为使变锋利，最早记录于十五世纪。

items.en: Modern English extends the verb to skills, emotions, conflicts, and photography, and sharpening a picture becomes an everyday digital task.
items.cn: 现代英语把这一动词扩展到技能、情绪、冲突与摄影领域，给影像锐化也成了日常的数字操作。

note.en: Sharpen is a causative verb built from sharp, with a family of sharpeners and sharpenings, and in meaning it sits near hone, whet, grind, and intensify.
note.cn: sharpen 是由 sharp 派生的使役动词，附近有 sharpener、sharpening 等词族，在意义上与 hone、whet、grind、intensify 相邻。

entries.definition: having a fine edge or point, or quick to notice
entries.definitionCN: 有锋刃或尖端的；敏锐的，是 sharpen 去掉 -en 之后的基础形容词

entries.definition: a tool for making pencils or blades sharp
entries.definitionCN: 削铅笔或磨刀的工具，由 sharpen 加 -er 构成

entries.definition: to make or become deeper
entries.definitionCN: 加深，与 sharpen 同样用在形容词后加 -en 构成

entries.definition: to make a blade or a skill finer and more effective
entries.definitionCN: 把刀刃或技能磨得更精，比 sharpen 更强调精细地修整

entries.definition: to sharpen a blade, or to excite an appetite
entries.definitionCN: 磨刀；激起胃口或兴趣，常用于 whet the appetite

entries.definition: to press and rub a surface, sometimes to sharpen or smooth it
entries.definitionCN: 研磨；打磨，动作比 sharpen 更用力，也常指把东西磨碎

normalIntro.en: Sharpen is the ordinary verb of putting an edge on something, and it is built the same way as widen and deepen.
normalIntro.cn: sharpen 是「把东西弄出锋刃」的普通动词，构词方式和 widen、deepen 一样。

normal.en: Sharpen a pencil is a task at the start of every drawing lesson.
normal.cn: sharpen a pencil 是每堂画画课开始时都要做的事。

normal.en: A sharpener is the small tool that holds the blade; it is sharpen plus -er.
normal.cn: sharpener 就是装着刀刃的小文具，即 sharpen 加 -er。

normal.en: Sharpen your skills means to practise until you are better.
normal.cn: sharpen your skills 意为反复练习直到更熟练。

normal.en: Words like widen, deepen, and lengthen show the same pattern as sharpen.
normal.cn: widen、deepen、lengthen 这些词与 sharpen 遵循同一构词模式。

normal.en: Compare hone: hone is a finer, more careful repair of an already good edge, sharpen is the broader verb.
normal.cn: 对比 hone：hone 是对已经很不错的锋刃做更细致修整，sharpen 更宽泛。

abstract.en: Picture the blade drawn across the stone, again and again, until the light runs along it.
abstract.cn: 想象刀刃在磨石上拉了又拉，直到光顺着刃口一路滑下去。

abstract.en: Picture a pencil tip turning from blunt grey to fine dark point.
abstract.cn: 想象铅笔尖从灰钝的一截，变成又细又黑的一个点。

abstract.en: Picture the photo on a screen suddenly snapping into focus.
abstract.cn: 想象屏幕上的照片忽然变得清晰锐利。

examples.en: It is easier to cut cloth with a sharpened pair of scissors.
examples.cn: 用磨快的剪刀剪布更容易。

examples.en: Reading widely sharpens the mind.
examples.cn: 广泛阅读能磨砺头脑。

examples.en: The rescue effort sharpened after the second earthquake struck.
examples.cn: 第二次地震发生后，救援工作变得更加紧迫。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「煞」加「喷」——刀刃「煞」的一下喷出金属火星，就是磨快了；谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 scearp（锐利的、严厉的），远源为日耳曼语中表示切割的语根；英语在十五世纪用「形容词 + -en」的模式造出 sharpen，意为「使变锋利」，词根义始终是「切割」。

sensesIntro.en: Sharpen starts from the physical edge of a blade, then puts the same edge on tips, skills, feelings, images, and rising prices.
sensesIntro.cn: sharpen 从刀刃的物理锋刃出发，再把同一份「锐」加到尖端、技能、情绪、影像与上扬的价格上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: steel pressed against a grindstone until a thin bright edge appears.
core.cn: 核心意象：钢刃压在磨石上，直到磨出一道细亮的口子。

branches.en: Blades and pencil tips are the two literal outcomes of grinding a sharp edge.
branches.cn: 刀刃与铅笔尖是磨出锋刃这一动作最字面的两个结果。

branches.en: A trained mind is an edge made keen by practice.
branches.cn: 受过训练的头脑就是靠练习磨锐的锋刃。

branches.en: Stronger emotion follows from a deeper cut.
branches.cn: 情绪变强，来自刀口划得更深。

branches.en: A clear image is a crisp edge in light.
branches.cn: 清晰的影像就是光线下利落分明的边界。

branches.en: Steep price lines rise like the slope of a blade.
branches.cn: 陡峭的价格线像刀刃的斜面一样翘起。

intro.en: Sharpen shows the productive English pattern of adjective plus -en, the same one behind widen, deepen, and quicken; the adjective sharp in turn comes from Old English with no borrowed affix.
intro.cn: sharpen 体现英语里「形容词 + -en」的能产模式，与 widen、deepen、quicken 相同；而形容词 sharp 本身继承自古英语，没有借入的词缀。

latinIntro.en: Sharpen is Germanic and has no Latin ancestor; Latin expressed the sharpening of a blade with acuere, whose root survives in acumen and acute, but those words are cousins in meaning only.
latinIntro.cn: sharpen 属日耳曼语源，没有拉丁语祖源；拉丁语用 acuere 表示磨刀，其词根留在 acumen 与 acute 里，但这些词只是意义上的远亲。

items.meaning: having a fine edge or point
items.example: Sharp is the core of the family.
items.exampleCN: sharp 是整个词族的核心。

items.example: The suffix -en turns sharp into sharpen.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -en 把 sharp 变成 sharpen。

items.example: Sharpen is a causative verb.
items.exampleCN: sharpen 是一个使役动词。

items.meaning: a person or thing that does
items.meaningCN: 表示施加动作的人或物的词尾
items.example: The suffix -er forms sharpener.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -er 构成 sharpener。

items.meaning: a tool that makes things sharp
items.example: A pencil sharpener sits on the desk.
items.exampleCN: 桌上放着一个削笔刀。

items.example: The suffix -ness forms sharpness.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ness 构成 sharpness。

items.example: Sharpness of eye helps a proofreader.
items.exampleCN: 眼力敏锐有助于校对工作。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms sharply.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 sharply。

items.meaning: in a sharp or sudden way
items.example: Prices rose sharply last spring.
items.exampleCN: 去年春天价格急剧上涨。

items.meaningCN: 表示活动或过程的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ing forms sharpening.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 构成 sharpening。

latinEntries.example: Latin acuere means to sharpen, but is not the source of sharpen.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 acuere 意为磨快，但并不是 sharpen 的来源。

latinEntries.example: Acumen from acuere is a cousin in meaning, not in form.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 来自 acuere 的 acumen 只是在意义上相近，并非同形同源。

latinEntries.example: Acutus lies behind the English word acute.
latinEntries.exampleCN: acute 一词可上溯到 acutus。

definition_zh: 打碎；粉碎；破灭；摧毁；使...崩溃；碎裂声
definition_en: to break something suddenly into many small pieces, and by extension to destroy a hope or to leave a person deeply shaken
core_image: 玻璃杯落地的一瞬，碎片带着脆响四散飞开
scene: 餐厅里有人托盘不稳，杯子从桌面滑落，在地上摔成许多细小的碎片。A waiter lost his grip and the glass shattered on the tiled floor.
sceneCN: 这里 shattered 是「摔碎」（第 1 个义项：猛地分成许多碎片）；句意：一名服务员没拿稳，玻璃杯摔在瓷砖地上碎了。

pos.zh: 打碎；粉碎；使破灭；使崩溃
碎片；碎裂声

derivatives.zh: 由现在分词转化的形容词，义为「令人震惊的；毁灭性的」，也可作名词指「碎裂」
过去分词转化的形容词，义为「破碎的；震惊的；筋疲力尽的」
shatter 与表示「防……」的后缀 -proof 合成，义为「防碎的」

senses.title: To break into many small pieces
senses.definition: to break suddenly and violently into many separate pieces
senses.definitionCN: 突然猛烈地裂成许多碎块
senses.example: The bottle shattered against the wall.
senses.exampleCN: 瓶子撞在墙上碎掉了。
senses.why: The word is probably imitative of a crash, so the sound of breaking is built into the meaning.
senses.whyCN: 这个词很可能模仿碎裂的巨响，所以「破成碎片」的声音本身就写进了词义。

senses.title: To destroy a hope or a plan
senses.definition: to destroy a hope, a trust, or a plan completely so that nothing remains
senses.definitionCN: 彻底摧毁希望、信任或计划，不留下任何余地
senses.example: One bad decision shattered his confidence.
senses.exampleCN: 一个糟糕的决定摧毁了他的信心。
senses.why: A hope is like a glass held in the hand, and once it is dropped the pieces cannot be put together again.
senses.whyCN: 希望像手里的一只杯子，掉下去就成了碎片，再也拼不起来，于是打碎的动作借来指希望破灭。

senses.title: To shake someone deeply
senses.definition: to make someone feel extremely upset or shocked, so that they can hardly cope
senses.definitionCN: 使某人极度难过或震惊，几乎无法应对
senses.example: The court verdict left the family shattered.
senses.exampleCN: 法庭的裁决让这家人彻底崩溃了。
senses.why: When something inside you shatters, calm and routine break up just like glass on the floor.
senses.whyCN: 当体内有什么东西碎裂时，平静与日常就像地上的玻璃一样散了一地。

senses.title: To break a record or a barrier
senses.definition: to break a record, a limit, or an old belief completely and suddenly
senses.definitionCN: 彻底而突然地打破纪录、界限或旧有看法
senses.example: The film shattered box-office records in its first week.
senses.exampleCN: 这部电影上映第一周就打破了票房纪录。
senses.why: A limit that seemed solid is smashed all at once, so shatter suits a record that falls by a wide margin.
senses.whyCN: 看上去牢固的界限一下子被砸开，所以 shatter 适合形容大幅打破纪录。

senses.title: To interrupt a silence
senses.definition: used of a sound, to break the quiet of a place in a sudden and shocking way
senses.definitionCN: 用于声音，指突然而惊人地打破某处的安静
senses.example: A single scream shattered the silence of the night.
senses.exampleCN: 一声尖叫打破了夜晚的寂静。
senses.why: The stillness of a room is treated as something fragile, and one loud noise can smash it.
senses.whyCN: 屋里的安静被当成一样易碎之物，一声巨响就能把它砸开。

senses.title: Fragments of something broken
senses.definition: the broken pieces of something, especially glass, often used in the plural as shatters
senses.definitionCN: 某物破碎后的碎片，尤指玻璃，复数形式为 shatters
senses.example: Workers swept up the shatters of the fallen lampshade.
senses.exampleCN: 工人们把掉落灯罩的碎片扫走了。
senses.why: The verb, like many English verbs, was borrowed as a noun so that the result of breaking could be named.
senses.whyCN: 和许多英语动词一样，这个词也被借作名词，好用来指破碎之后留下的结果。

intro.en: Shatter appears in Middle English as schateren or schater, most likely imitative of the sound of shattering, with no certain Latin or Old English ancestor.
intro.cn: shatter 在中古英语写作 schateren 或 schater，很可能模仿碎裂声而成，没有确切的拉丁语或古英语祖源。

items.en: Schateren and schater are recorded in Middle English with the sense of scattering or breaking apart, often of hard things.
items.cn: 中古英语记录有 schateren、schater，意为四散、裂开，多用于坚硬的东西。

items.en: Many reference works treat the word as sound-imitative, related to North Sea Germanic forms such as shatter and scatter, though this is argued rather than agreed.
items.cn: 不少辞书认为这个词是拟声词，与 shatter、scatter 等北海日耳曼语形式有关，但这只是有争议的假说，并非共识。

items.en: The word settles into the spelling shatter and adds the figurative sense of breaking a plan or a hope.
items.cn: 词形固定为 shatter，并增加「使计划或希望破灭」的比喻义。

items.en: The past participle shattered is used of a body or a mind left in pieces, and so comes to mean shocked or utterly worn out.
items.cn: 过去分词 shattered 被用来形容身体或心智散成碎片，于是转而表示震惊或极度疲惫。

items.en: Modern English shatters records and silence as easily as glass, and wears a shatterproof screen on a phone.
items.cn: 现代英语可以像打碎玻璃一样打破纪录、打破寂静，手机上也装着防碎的屏幕。

note.en: Shatter has a small family of forms such as shattered and shattering, and in meaning it sits near smash, crack, and fragment on the physical side and ruin on the figurative side.
note.cn: shatter 有 shattered、shattering 等少量派生形式，意义上与 smash、crack、fragment 在物理层面相邻，也与 ruin 在比喻层面相邻。

entries.definition: to throw pieces or people in different directions
entries.definitionCN: 把东西或人抛向各个方向；只是拼写相近，词源不同，sh- 与 sc- 的首音容易混淆

entries.definition: broken into pieces, or deeply shocked and tired
entries.definitionCN: 破碎的；受到极大打击或疲惫不堪的，由过去分词转成形容词

entries.definition: very shocking or destructive
entries.definitionCN: 令人震惊的；毁灭性的，由现在分词转成形容词

entries.definition: to break something violently into pieces with a loud noise
entries.definitionCN: 猛烈击打使东西碎裂，并发出响声，动作比 shatter 更强调击打的力

entries.definition: to break a line across a surface without falling apart
entries.definitionCN: 在表面裂开一条缝，但尚未碎散，破坏程度比 shatter 轻得多

entries.definition: to break into small parts, or a small broken part
entries.definitionCN: 碎裂成分小块，或指碎片本身，比 shatter 更正式、也更常见于书面说明

normalIntro.en: Shatter is a short crashing verb whose beginning sounds like the smash itself, and it holds one form for past and participle: shattered.
normalIntro.cn: shatter 是个短促的撞击动词，开头的声音就像碰撞本身，过去式与过去分词同形，都是 shattered。

normal.en: Shattered glass is the everyday phrase: the window, the mirror, the bottle on the floor.
normal.cn: shattered glass 是常用说法：窗户、镜子、地上的瓶子。

normal.en: Shatter a record means to beat it by a wide margin.
normal.cn: shatter a record 意为以很大差距打破纪录。

normal.en: Shatterproof is shatter plus -proof, as in waterproof and fireproof.
normal.cn: shatterproof 是 shatter 加 -proof，和 waterproof、fireproof 同一构词法。

normal.en: Shattered as an adjective often means exhausted: I felt completely shattered after the flight.
normal.cn: shattered 作形容词常表示疲惫：长途飞行后我觉得完全散架了。

normal.en: Compare break: break is general and gentle, shatter is sudden and leaves many pieces, break a leg but shatter a mirror.
normal.cn: 对比 break：break 更普通也更温和，shatter 突然且留下许多碎片，腿可以 break，镜子则常 shatter。

abstract.en: Picture a glass dropping from a table edge and bursting into dozens of small pieces.
abstract.cn: 想象一只杯子从桌边滑落，炸成几十块小碎片。

abstract.en: Picture a mirror on the floor, and in every piece a separate face.
abstract.cn: 想象地上的一面碎镜，每一块碎片里都有一张脸。

abstract.en: Picture a night of silence torn open by one shout.
abstract.cn: 想象寂静的夜里，被一声喊叫撕开。

examples.en: The hail shattered the greenhouse windows.
examples.cn: 冰雹砸碎了温室的窗户。

examples.en: The news shattered her plans for the summer.
examples.cn: 这个消息粉碎了她对夏天的计划。

examples.en: He was shattered after working a double shift.
examples.cn: 他连上两个班之后累得筋疲力尽。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「砂踏」——砂石被一脚踏下去，碎成一片细渣，所以 shatter 是打碎；谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 中古英语 schateren、schater（四散、碎裂），一般认为来源于拟声，与 scatter 等北海日耳曼语形式有关，但词源尚无定论；核心义「猛力破成碎片」。

sensesIntro.en: Shatter begins with glass breaking into many pieces, then breaks hopes, nerves, records, and silence in the same sudden way.
sensesIntro.cn: shatter 起于玻璃碎成许多小块，随后以同样的猛烈方式打碎希望、神经、纪录与寂静。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a glass striking the floor and bursting outward in fragments.
core.cn: 核心意象：玻璃杯砸在地上，碎片向外炸开。

branches.en: The physical breaking and the pieces it leaves are the literal senses.
branches.cn: 物理上的碎裂以及留下的碎片是最字面的义项。

branches.en: A hope breaks the way a glass does: suddenly, and beyond repair.
branches.cn: 希望像玻璃一样碎裂：突然，而且无法修复。

branches.en: A shattered person has something inside broken by shock.
branches.cn: 崩溃的人，是内心被震惊击碎了一样东西。

branches.en: A record that is beaten by a wide margin is smashed rather than merely passed.
branches.cn: 被大幅超越的纪录是被砸碎，而不只是被超越。

branches.en: Silence is another fragile surface that one loud sound can break.
branches.cn: 寂静是另一层易碎的表面，一声巨响就能把它打破。

intro.en: Shatter is a single imitative stem with no borrowed prefix; the English words around it are built with -ed, -ing, and the combining form -proof.
intro.cn: shatter 是单独一个拟声词干，没有借入的前缀；围绕它的英语词由 -ed、-ing 与组合形式 -proof 构成。

latinIntro.en: Shatter has no Latin ancestor; Latin described breaking with frangere, from which fragile and fracture come, and those words are relatives in meaning only.
latinIntro.cn: shatter 没有拉丁语祖源；拉丁语用 frangere 表示打碎，fragile 与 fracture 由此而来，这些词只在意义上与它相近。

items.example: Shatter is the core verb of the group.
items.exampleCN: shatter 是这一群体的核心动词。

items.meaningCN: 过去式与过去分词的词尾
items.example: The glass shattered on the floor.
items.exampleCN: 玻璃杯在地上碎了。

items.example: She was shattered by the news.
items.exampleCN: 她被这个消息击垮了。

items.meaning: present participle or noun of action
items.meaningCN: 现在分词或表示动作的名词词尾
items.example: The shattering of the window woke us.
items.exampleCN: 窗户碎裂的声音把我们吵醒了。

items.example: It was a shattering defeat.
items.exampleCN: 那是一场毁灭性的失败。

items.example: The suffix -proof turns shatter into shatterproof.
items.exampleCN: 组合形式 -proof 把 shatter 变成 shatterproof。

items.meaning: not able to be broken easily
items.example: The screen is shatterproof glass.
items.exampleCN: 这块屏幕是防碎玻璃。

items.example: Scatter looks like shatter but has a separate history.
items.exampleCN: scatter 看起来像 shatter，但来历不同。

items.example: Smash and shatter both imitate a crash.
items.exampleCN: smash 与 shatter 都带有撞碎的声响感。

latinEntries.example: Latin frangere means to break but is not the source of shatter.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 frangere 意为打碎，但并不是 shatter 的来源。

latinEntries.example: Fragilis gives the English word fragile.
Fractura gives the English word fracture.

definition_zh: 披肩；披巾；（方形或长条的）大围巾
definition_en: a large square or long piece of cloth that is worn loosely over the shoulders, the upper body or the head, often as an extra layer of warmth
core_image: 一大方软布斜披在肩上，两角垂在胸前
scene: 高原的清晨很冷，祖母从木箱里取出一条厚羊毛大布，给快要出门的孩子裹在想去的集市路上。Grandmother draped a thick wool shawl over the boy shoulders and pinned it at the front.
sceneCN: 这里 shawl 是「披肩、披巾」（第 1 个义项：披在肩上或头上、用来保暖的大块布）；句意：祖母把一条厚羊毛披肩披在男孩肩上，又在胸前别好。它不缝袖子，只靠披挂挡住肩上的寒气。

pos.zh: 披肩；披巾；大围巾
用披肩裹住

derivatives.zh: 由本词加词尾 -ed 构成，义为「披着披肩的」
由本词与 collar 合成，义为「披肩领的」，如 shawl-collar coat 披肩领大衣
织入花纹的面料；broche shawl 指带织纹的披巾，broche 与新词同源，都来自表达「扎、别」的古代词根

senses.title: A large cloth for the shoulders
senses.definition: a large square or long cloth that is worn loosely over the shoulders and is not sewn into a coat
senses.definitionCN: 一大块方形或长条形软布，松松披在肩上，并不缝成外套
senses.example: She draped a woollen shawl over her shoulders and stepped out into the cold.
senses.exampleCN: 她把一条羊毛披肩披在肩上，走进寒风中。
senses.why: The word names a long piece of cloth first, so the shawl is simply a big sheet of fabric that the body carries instead of a garment that the body wears as a whole.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最早指一整块长布，所以披肩就是被身体扛着走的一大块布，而不是把身体整个包起来的衣服。

senses.title: A cloth pulled over the head
senses.definition: the same kind of large cloth, drawn up over the head and sometimes the face as well
senses.definitionCN: 同一种大块布，被拉起来罩住头和脸
senses.example: The old woman covered her grey hair with a black shawl before she walked into the wind.
senses.exampleCN: 老妇人走进风里之前，用一条黑色头巾盖住了满头白发。
senses.why: A cloth wide enough for the shoulders is also wide enough for the head, so the same word took on the head covering, especially in cold, dusty or windy places.
senses.whyCN: 能盖住肩的布当然也盖得住头，所以同一个词又指头巾，尤其在寒冷、多尘或刮风的地方。

senses.title: The fine patterned shawl of the East
senses.definition: a fine, hand-woven shawl, often of fine goat wool and often with woven patterns, such as the Kashmir and paisley shawls of the nineteenth century
senses.definitionCN: 精细手工织成的披巾，多用山羊绒，常织出花纹，如十九世纪的克什米尔披巾与佩斯利披巾
senses.example: The paisley shawl became a prized fashion item across Europe in the early nineteenth century.
senses.exampleCN: 十九世纪初，佩斯利披巾成了整个欧洲追捧的时尚品。
senses.why: In Persian the word was a fine woven cloth, so in English it came first to mean the expensive patterned shawls traded from Kashmir, and only later the everyday warm shawl.
senses.whyCN: 在波斯语里这个词指精细织物，所以英语先用它称呼从克什米尔远道运来的花披巾，后来才泛指日常保暖的披肩。

senses.title: A cloth wrapped round a baby
senses.definition: a piece of cloth in which a baby is loosely wrapped to keep it warm or to carry it
senses.definitionCN: 用来把婴儿松松裹住、保暖或抱在怀里的布
senses.example: The baby was carried in a shawl tied across her mother back.
senses.exampleCN: 婴儿被一条披巾裹着，扎在母亲背上。
senses.why: Where a big soft cloth covers the shoulders, it can also cover and hold a small body, so the shawl became a baby wrap in many cultures.
senses.whyCN: 大块软布既能盖肩，也能包住小小的身体，于是在许多文化里披巾又成了包婴儿的襁褓。

senses.title: The draped collar of a jacket
senses.definition: a wide, soft, rounded collar that rolls from the back of the neck down the front of a coat or cardigan
senses.definitionCN: 从后颈两侧向前翻滚成宽弧、显得柔软的领子，常见于大衣或开衫
senses.example: A shawl collar on a cardigan adds a touch of luxury to a very simple jacket.
senses.exampleCN: 开衫上的披肩领给一件很简单的外套添了几分贵气。
senses.why: The rolled collar hangs like a shawl falling from the neck, so tailors borrowed the name of the cloth for the shape it makes.
senses.whyCN: 翻卷的领子垂在身侧，就像一块从颈部落下的披巾，于是裁缝把这块布的名字借去称呼它的形状。

senses.title: To shawl somebody up
senses.definition: to wrap or cover a person or thing in a shawl or something like one
senses.definitionCN: 用披肩或类似的东西把人或物裹住、盖住
senses.example: She shawled the sleeping child up against the night air.
senses.exampleCN: 她用披巾把睡着的小孩裹紧，挡住夜里的凉气。
senses.why: Once the noun named the cloth, English used it as a verb for the act of putting that cloth on someone.
senses.whyCN: 名词先固定指这块布，英语随后就把它当动词用，表示把这块布裹到某人身上这个动作。

senses.title: A broad cloak or mantle
senses.definition: a broad cloth garment with or without sleeves, worn outdoors as an outer covering, as in the long travellers shawls of older English tales
senses.definitionCN: 宽大、有无袖子都可以的外披衣物，如旧时故事中旅人穿的长披风
senses.example: The rider threw a heavy travelling shawl over his coat when the first snow came.
senses.exampleCN: 初雪落下时，骑手把一件厚重的大披风披在外套外面。
senses.why: Older and looser usage let the word spread from the shoulder cloth to any large outer wrap, so travellers carried a shawl that was close to a cloak.
senses.whyCN: 较早而较宽的用法让这个词从肩布扩展到各种宽大的外披，旅人带的披巾几乎就是一件斗篷。

intro.en: Shawl was taken into English in the seventeenth century from Persian shal, the word for a fine woven cloth, which tradition links to Sanskrit terms for cloth.
intro.cn: shawl 于十七世纪从波斯语 shal 进入英语，本义是精细织物，一般认为可追溯到梵语中表示布匹的词，与南亚的莎丽同出一系。

items.en: Sanskrit sati or satika is often reconstructed as the cloth term behind the Persian word; this link is generally accepted but not certain.
items.cn: 一般认为波斯语借自梵语中表示布的 sati 或 satika；这一关联通行接受，但并非定论。

items.en: Persian shal names a fine woven cloth, especially the shawls worked in the Kashmir region.
items.cn: 波斯语 shal 指精细织物，尤其指克什米尔地区织成的披巾。

items.en: The Persian word reached European traders in forms such as shal, and this is the usual route through which English met it.
items.cn: 波斯语词以 shal 一类的形式传到欧洲商人口中，英语通常正是经由这条路线接触到它。

items.en: Shawl is first recorded in English about 1662, naming the imported patterned shawl from India and Persia.
items.cn: shawl 约在 1662 年首次见于英语记录，指从印度与波斯进口的花纹披巾。

items.en: Kashmir shawls became a European luxury, woven from fine goat wool, and mills in Scotland and France copied them.
items.cn: 克什米尔披巾成为欧洲奢侈品，用细腻的山羊绒织成，苏格兰与法国的织厂纷纷仿制。

items.en: The word widened to any large warm shoulder cloth, to head coverings and baby wraps, and to the shawl collar of a jacket.
items.cn: 这个词扩展到任何保暖的大块肩布、头巾与襁褓布，也指外套上的披肩领。

note.en: Shawl belongs to the family of draped and wrapped cloths, and in meaning it stands near stole, poncho and cloak.
note.cn: shawl 属于「披挂、包裹的布」这一族，在意义上靠近 stole、poncho 与 cloak。

entries.definition: a unit of money no longer in use in modern trade
entries.definitionCN: 一种早已不再流通的货币单位；只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: a long piece of cloth worn around the neck or the head
entries.definitionCN: 围巾，长条布围在颈上或头上；只是发音略近，词源不同

entries.definition: wearing or wrapped in a shawl
entries.definitionCN: 披着披肩的；由本词加词尾构成

entries.definition: a long scarf-like strip of cloth worn over the shoulders
entries.definitionCN: 披在肩上的长条披带；与披肩同类，但更窄更轻

entries.definition: a piece of cloth with a hole for the head, worn as a cape
entries.definitionCN: 中间开洞、套头穿的斗篷式披巾

entries.definition: a loose outer garment worn over other clothes
entries.definitionCN: 披在外面的宽松斗篷；比披肩更像整件衣服

normalIntro.en: Shawl is a Persian cloth word that became English everyday: first the costly patterned shawls of Kashmir, then any big warm cloth that sits on the shoulders.
normalIntro.cn: shawl 是一个波斯语布料词变成的日常英语词：先指昂贵的克什米尔花纹披巾，后来泛指任何披在肩上的大块暖布。

normal.en: The Persian word behind it means a fine woven cloth, so a shawl is cloth before it is a garment.
normal.cn: 它的波斯语源头意为精细织物，所以披肩首先是一块布，其次才是一件衣服。

normal.en: A shawl collar is named for the shawl shape: the collar rolls down the front like a cloth falling off the neck.
normal.cn: 披肩领得名于披肩的形状：领子顺着前襟翻滚而下，就像一块布从颈部垂落。

normal.en: The verb is simple: to shawl someone means to put a shawl on them.
normal.cn: 动词用法很简单：to shawl someone 就是给某人披上披肩。

normal.en: Say it with its partners: drape a shawl, wrap up in a shawl, a woollen shawl.
normal.cn: 和常用的伙伴一起记：drape a shawl 披上披巾、wrap up in a shawl 裹进披肩、a woollen shawl 羊毛披肩。

normal.en: Compare scarf: a scarf is narrow and goes round the neck, while a shawl is wide and goes over the shoulders.
normal.cn: 对比 scarf：围巾窄，绕在脖子上；披肩宽，盖在肩膀上。

abstract.en: Picture a patterned shawl held out flat, two corners in each hand as wide as the arms can stretch.
abstract.cn: 想象把一条花纹披巾平直地展开，两角分握在手中，宽得和张开的两臂一样。

abstract.en: Picture the same cloth pulled up over a head bent against the wind.
abstract.cn: 想象同一块布被拉起来罩住低下去迎风的头。

abstract.en: Picture a coat collar that rolls down the front, gently rounded like a soft shawl.
abstract.cn: 想象一件大衣的领子顺着前襟翻卷而下，圆润柔顺，像一条软披巾。

examples.en: Grandmother always kept a woollen shawl by the door for cold mornings.
examples.cn: 祖母总在门口放一条羊毛披肩，留给寒冷的早晨。

examples.en: The web of fine patterned shawls traded from Kashmir reached London in the nineteenth century.
examples.cn: 十九世纪，从克什米尔贩运来的精细花纹披巾进入了伦敦市场。

examples.en: She shawled the wailing baby and carried him to the door.
examples.cn: 她用披巾把哭闹的婴儿裹好，抱到了门口。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「销了」——披巾一披上面子就挂不住，干脆销了；这只是谐音联想，与波斯语 shal 无关。

root: 波斯语 shal（精细织物、披巾）→ 英语 shawl（披巾；披肩）；一般认为更早源出梵语中表示布匹的词，与莎丽 sari 同系。核心义是「披挂在肩上的大块布」。

sensesIntro.en: Shawl begins as a fine cloth from Persia and Kashmir, then covers the head and warms the shoulders, and finally spreads to a baby wrap, a collar shape and a verb.
sensesIntro.cn: shawl 起初指来自波斯与克什米尔的精细布匹，后来既保暖肩背又罩住头，最后扩展到襁褓布、领型与动词用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a large square of soft cloth draped over both shoulders, with the two corners hanging at the front.
core.cn: 核心意象：一大方正软布斜披在两肩上，两个角垂在胸前。

branches.en: BODY LINE: the shoulder cloth is the everyday sense of the word.
branches.cn: 身体线：披在肩上的布是这个词最日常的义项。

branches.en: SOURCE LINE: the Persian fine cloth and its fine patterned shawls are where the English word came from.
branches.cn: 来源线：波斯精细织物及克什米尔花纹披巾正是英语这个词的来源。

branches.en: SMALL BODY LINE: the same cloth is wrapped round a baby to carry it.
branches.cn: 小身体线：同一块布裹住婴儿，方便把他抱在怀里。

branches.en: SHAPE LINE: the collar that rolls like a falling cloth borrows the name.
branches.cn: 形状线：翻卷如落布的领子借用了这个词的名字。

branches.en: ACTION AND WIDTH: the cloth becomes a verb, and older English used it for any broad outer wrap.
branches.cn: 动作与宽度：这块布变成了动词，较早的英语也用它指各种宽大的外披。

intro.en: Shawl is a whole cloth loanword with almost no affixes of its own; English builds its few forms with the endings -ed and -s and by compounding with collar, while the deeper root shows in the related word broche.
intro.cn: shawl 是一个整词借来的布料词，本身几乎没有词缀可拆；英语只用词尾 -ed、复数 -s 以及和 collar 合成的办法造出少数形式，更早的词根则体现在同源词 broche 上。

latinIntro.en: The word came from Persian rather than Latin, so there are no Latin cognates; the older root behind it is reconstructed as bhrāk, to rub or to pierce.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词来自波斯语而非拉丁语，因此没有拉丁同源词；它更古老的词根一般重构为 bhrāk，意为摩擦或穿透。

items.meaning: a large cloth worn over the shoulders
items.example: Shawl keeps the whole cloth as one word.
items.exampleCN: shawl 把整块布的名称整套保留为一个词。

items.meaning: a fine woven cloth, a shawl
items.example: Persian shal is the direct source of the English word.
items.exampleCN: 波斯语 shal 是英语这个词的直接来源。

items.meaningCN: 布条；布匹（一般认为的来源形式）
items.example: The Sanskrit cloth term is usually given as sati or satika, the older form behind the Persian word.
items.exampleCN: 一般认为梵语的布料词写作 sati 或 satika，是波斯语词背后更古老的形式。

items.example: The ending -s turns shawl into shawls.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -s 把 shawl 变成 shawls。

items.example: The ending -ed forms shawled, meaning wrapped in a shawl.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ed 构成 shawled，意为披着披肩的。

items.example: Shawl plus collar names a collar shaped like a draped cloth.
items.exampleCN: shawl 与 collar 合成，指形状像披挂之布的领子。

items.example: A shawl-collar cardigan is named after the collar it has.
items.exampleCN: shawl-collar cardigan 披肩领开衫就是按它的领子命名的。

items.meaning: a woven fabric with a raised pattern
items.example: Broche and shawl both trace back to the older cloth root.
items.exampleCN: broche 与 shawl 都追溯到更古老的布料词根。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加词尾 -ed 构成，义为「披着披肩的」
由本词与 collar 合成，义为「披肩领的」

definition_zh: 托儿；受雇冒充顾客或普通用户、暗中替某方吹捧的人
definition_en: a person who is paid or planted to pose as an ordinary, independent customer or supporter and so persuade other people to buy something or take a side
core_image: 人群里一个被雇来的「顾客」，举手出价、大声叫好，装作与卖家毫无关系
scene: 夜市的摊位前围了一圈人，一个陌生面孔举起刚买的货，大声说自己也刚抢到一个，好让围观的人跟着掏钱。A shill at the night stall kept calling the goods a bargain and pushing the crowd to pay.
sceneCN: 这里 shill 是「托儿」（第 1 个义项：受雇冒充顾客、暗中替卖家拉生意的人）；句意：夜市摊位旁的托儿不停吆喝货物便宜，催着人群掏钱。他举手、叫好的样子都和真顾客一样，却不露半点受雇的痕迹。

pos.zh: 托儿；雇用骗子；冒名吹捧者
当托儿；替……吹捧；抬价

collocations.zh: 替某个行业当托儿的人

derivatives.zh: 由动词加名词后缀 -ing 构成，义为当托儿、托价的行为，如 shill bidding 自抬竞价；注意同形的 shilling 也指旧时英国的先令，二者词源不同
由本词与 bid 合成，义为卖家安排的虚假出价，用来抬高价格
由 shill 与 bidder 合成，义为受雇假竞拍、把价格往上顶的人

senses.title: A paid fake customer
senses.definition: someone planted in a crowd or an audience to act like an ordinary eager buyer or supporter, while secretly being paid by the seller or promoter
senses.definitionCN: 被安插在人群或观众中、假装成热心普通顾客或支持者的人，实际上由卖家或推手暗中付钱
senses.example: One of the customers who kept praising the watch turned out to be a shill paid by the stall.
senses.exampleCN: 那些一直夸这块手表好的顾客之一，后来被查出是摊主雇来的托儿。
senses.why: The word first names a helper who pretends to be a stranger, so the heart of the meaning is the disguise, not the praise itself.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最早指一个假装成路人的帮手，所以它的核心在「伪装」，而不在夸奖本身。

senses.title: The auction and carnival accomplice
senses.definition: an accomplice at an auction, a gambling game or a fair booth who bids or plays to draw in real buyers and push up the price
senses.definitionCN: 在拍卖、赌局或游园摊位上配合作局的同伙，通过出价或下注招来真正的买家、把价钱往上抬
senses.example: The auctioneer used a shill in the back row to push the bids higher.
senses.exampleCN: 拍卖师安排了一名托儿坐在后排，把出价一路抬高。
senses.why: In this older setting the shill is an accomplice rather than a passer-by, but the trick is the same: the crowd must believe that someone else really wants the goods.
senses.whyCN: 在这个较早的场景里，托儿是同伙而不是路人，但手法一样：必须让围观的人相信真有人想要这件货。

senses.title: A paid promoter posing as an expert
senses.titleCN: 受雇吹捧者；（网络上的）水军
senses.definition: a person or an account paid to endorse a product, a cause or a public figure while appearing to be an independent voice, such as on review sites and social media
senses.definitionCN: 受雇为某产品、某项主张或某位公众人物站台，却装成独立声音的人或账号，常见于点评网站与社交媒体
senses.example: Several five-star reviews were later traced to shills hired by the app maker.
senses.exampleCN: 有几条五星评论后来被查出是应用开发商雇来的水军写的。
senses.why: Review pages and social media merely moved the market stall online, so the disguise of being an ordinary customer survives in a new setting.
senses.whyCN: 点评页与社交媒体只是把摊位搬到了网上，冒充普通顾客的那层伪装也原封不动地延续下来。

senses.title: To promote as a shill
senses.definition: to praise, recommend or push a product or view in this paid and disguised way
senses.definitionCN: 以这种受雇且伪装的方式夸奖、推荐或推销某产品或某观点
senses.example: Celebrities are paid to shill everything from soft drinks to insurance.
senses.exampleCN: 名人们收了钱，从汽水到保险什么产品都替人卖了力吆喝。
senses.why: The noun turned into a verb easily, so the act of playing the shill is simply to shill.
senses.whyCN: 名词很容易变成动词，于是扮演托儿这个动作就直接叫 shill。

senses.title: A friendly cover charge
senses.titleCN: 朋友的「服务费」（俚语，已罕用）
senses.definition: a small friendly payment or cover charge among show business people; this old slang sense is now rare
senses.definitionCN: 演艺圈人士之间象征性的小额费用或「服务费」，这一旧俚语义现已罕用
senses.example: In the old days a performer might ask a friendly shill before going on stage.
senses.exampleCN: 过去，一位表演者在上台前也许会向熟人收一点象征性的钱。
senses.why: This rare slang sense is separate from the con-man sense, a reminder that one spelling can carry two unrelated histories, so it should not be used in modern writing.
senses.whyCN: 这个罕用俚语义与骗子义并不相干，正好提醒我们同一拼写可以承载两段无关的历史，因此现代写作中不宜使用。

senses.title: A sharp, high-pitched voice
senses.titleCN: 尖声的；刺耳的（拼写变体，已罕用）
senses.definition: an older spelling variant of shrill, meaning high and piercing in sound; it is now obsolete
senses.definitionCN: shrill（声音尖利刺耳）的旧拼写变体，现已废弃
senses.example: The old spelling appears in an early travel account with the meaning sharp to the ear.
senses.exampleCN: 这一旧拼写在早年的游记中以「刺耳」的含义出现。
senses.why: The -ill cluster of shrill was sometimes written shill by careless hands, so this sense is a spelling accident rather than a branch of the shill meaning.
senses.whyCN: shrill 中的 -ill 组合偶尔被写成 shill，所以这个义项只是拼写上的偶合，并不是「托儿」义的延伸。

senses.title: A plant or a stooge
senses.definition: a person placed in a group to act in secret for an outsider, close to the wider sense of plant or stooge
senses.definitionCN: 被安插在某个群体里、暗中替外人办事的人，接近 plant、stooge 这类词的广义用法
senses.example: The union suspected a shill among the volunteers who passed every complaint to the management.
senses.exampleCN: 工会怀疑志愿者当中有个暗桩，把每一条抱怨都转告给了管理层。
senses.why: A shill is only one kind of planted agent, so by extension the word can name any person hidden in a group to work for someone else.
senses.whyCN: 托儿只是暗桩的一种，因此这个词也可以引申指任何藏在群体里替别人办事的人。

intro.en: Shill for a decoy or an accomplice is first recorded in American English around the early twentieth century; its origin is uncertain.
intro.cn: shill 表示「托儿、雇来的骗子」的用法约在二十世纪初首次见于美式英语，词源存疑，尚无定论。

items.en: Dictionaries give no firm source for the decoy sense; often it is simply marked as origin unknown.
items.cn: 各家词典对「托儿」这一义都没有确定来源，通常只标注来源不明。

items.en: The word appears in American English early in the twentieth century, in the language of circuses, carnivals and confidence tricks.
items.cn: 这个词在二十世纪初见于美式英语，出现在马戏班、游园会与诈骗行当的用语里。

items.en: Many word books date the decoy sense to about 1914, while some mention an earlier appearance in print much closer to 1900.
items.cn: 许多词书把「托儿」义的年代定在 1914 年前后，也有资料提到它在更接近 1900 年的文献中已经出现，因此仅首次记载的年代存疑。

items.en: Carnival and gambling slang spread into ordinary American idiom, and shill began to name anyone who is paid to cheer or to bid.
items.cn: 游园会与赌局的俚语进入普通美式英语，shill 开始泛指任何受雇叫好或出价的人。

items.en: One frequently repeated guess derives it from the showman naming a small cover charge, but this story is not confirmed by records.
items.cn: 一种流传很广的猜测认为它出自演艺界对「小额服务费」的叫法，但文献并不支持这一说法。

items.en: Online reviews, social media and online auctions gave the word fresh life, and shill bidding is now a standard term in e-commerce.
items.cn: 网络点评、社交媒体与在线拍卖让这个词焕发新生，shill bidding 如今成了电商领域的标准用语。

note.en: Shill stands in the same field as decoy, stooge and plant, all names for a person placed where they are not supposed to be.
note.cn: shill 与 decoy、stooge、plant 同属「被安插的人」这一义场，都是指放在不该放的人身上的人。

entries.definition: high and piercing in sound
entries.definitionCN: 声音尖利刺耳的；只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: the hard outer covering of an egg, a nut or a shellfish
entries.definitionCN: 蛋壳、果壳或贝类的硬壳；只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: a flat board fixed to a wall for putting things on
entries.definitionCN: 钉在墙上的搁板；只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: a person who is used by another, often without real authority
entries.definitionCN: 受他人摆布的人；可指被利用的傀儡

entries.definition: a person or thing used to lure others into a trap
entries.definitionCN: 诱饵；引别人入圈套的人或物

entries.definition: a person placed in a group to work secretly for an outsider
entries.definitionCN: 安插在群体中的暗桩

normalIntro.en: Shill is a slang word of unknown origin, so learn it through its scenes: the fake customer at the stall, the hired bidder at the auction, the paid reviewer online.
normalIntro.cn: shill 是一个来源不明的俚语词，所以靠场景来记：摊位前假装的顾客、拍卖场里受雇的竞拍者、网络上有偿写出的好评。

normal.en: The word is marked origin unknown in dictionaries, so do not invent a root for it.
normal.cn: 词典对这个词的来源通常标注不明，因此不要凭空给它编词根。

normal.en: It is nearly always negative: a shill hides a business relationship and pretends to be an ordinary voice.
normal.cn: 它几乎总是贬义：托儿隐瞒与商家的关系，装成普通的声音。

normal.en: Common partner: shill for somebody or shill a product; the noun is often a shill for an industry.
normal.cn: 常见搭配：shill for somebody 替某人当托儿、shill a product 托某产品；名词常说 a shill for an industry 某行业的托儿。

normal.en: In auctions, shill bidding means planted bids that push prices up.
normal.cn: 在拍卖里，shill bidding 指安插的虚假出价把价格顶上去。

normal.en: Keep it apart from shilling: the money and the accent differ, and so do the histories.
normal.cn: 和 shilling 分清用法：一个是托价行为，一个是旧时货币，来源与含义都不相同。

abstract.en: Picture a man at a stall who looks like every other buyer but keeps glancing at the seller for a signal.
abstract.cn: 想象摊位前一个男人，外表和其他买家没两样，却不停朝摊主瞟一眼等示意。

abstract.en: Picture a hand in the back row of an auction hall going up on a private phone signal.
abstract.cn: 想象拍卖厅后排的一只手，全凭兜里手机的暗号举起牌子。

abstract.en: Picture a wall of five-star comments signed by accounts created on the same afternoon.
abstract.cn: 想象满屏五星好评，署名账号却全是同一个下午注册的。

examples.en: The reviewer was exposed as a shill who had been paid by the manufacturer.
examples.cn: 那位测评人被揭穿是个托儿，收了厂家的钱。

examples.en: Some online sellers pay fake bidders to shill the price of rare items.
examples.cn: 一些网络卖家雇假买家，把稀有物品的价格往上托。

examples.en: He would shill for any politician who promised him a reward.
examples.cn: 谁答应给他好处，他就替谁卖力吹捧。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「是尔」——托儿就是凑上前说「是尔家好货」的那个人；这只是谐音联想，与这个词不明的来源无关。

root: 来源不明（一般认为属美式俚语，二十世纪初见于马戏班与诈骗行话）→ shill（托儿；当托儿）。注意不要与 shrill、shell 强拉关系，也不要与旧货币词 shilling 混为一谈。

sensesIntro.en: Shill starts with the fake customer on the side of the seller, grows into the carnival and auction accomplice, and finally moves online as the paid reviewer, while two rare senses of very different history are left behind.
sensesIntro.cn: shill 从站在卖家一边的假顾客出发，发展为游园会与拍卖的同伙，最后上网变成有偿好评的水军，另有两个来源完全不同的罕用义项附在旁边。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hired stranger in the crowd who bids, buys and cheers as if they had no link to the seller.
core.cn: 核心意象：人群里一个被雇来的陌生人，出价、购买、叫好，装得和卖家毫无关系。

branches.en: STALL AND FAIR: the decoy who pretends to be an ordinary buyer, indoors and on the fairground.
branches.cn: 摊位与集市线：装作普通买家的托儿，出现在店铺里，也出现在游乐场上。

branches.en: ONLINE LINE: paid praise that hides its motive, and the verb for doing it.
branches.cn: 线上线：隐瞒动机的有偿夸赞，以及表示这一行为的动词。

branches.en: RARE EDGES: two old and obsolete senses that share only the spelling.
branches.cn: 罕用边缘：两个古老且已废弃的义项，与其他义项只共用一个拼写。

branches.en: WIDER LINE: any planted agent in a group, closer to plant and stooge.
branches.cn: 广义线：安插在群体里的暗桩，更接近 plant 与 stooge。

branches.en: DISGUISE: in every live sense the shill hides who really pays them.
branches.cn: 伪装线：在所有活跃义项里，托儿都隐藏了真正付钱的人是谁。

intro.en: Shill is a slang word of uncertain origin with no classical root to split, so the word families here come from English endings and compounds such as -ing, bid and bidder.
intro.cn: shill 是来源不明的俚语词，没有可拆的古典词根；这里的构词只能依靠英语词尾与复合，例如 -ing、bid 与 bidder。

latinIntro.en: No Latin or Persian source is known, so there are no cognate entries to add here.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词既没有可靠的拉丁语来源，也没有波斯语来源，因此没有同源词可供列出。

items.example: Shill comes into English as a single slang word.
items.exampleCN: shill 是作为一个整体俚语词进入英语的。

items.meaning: to promote by pretending to be independent
items.meaningCN: 伪装中立地替某方吹捧
items.example: The noun was turned into a verb without any change of form.
items.exampleCN: 名词不经任何形式变化就转成了动词。

items.meaning: more than one; third person singular
items.example: The ending -s gives shills for both the noun and the verb.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -s 既构成名词复数 shills，也构成动词三单 shills。

items.example: The ending -ed forms shilled.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ed 构成 shilled。

items.example: The ending -ing forms shilling, the act of playing the shill.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 构成 shilling，指当托儿的行为。

items.meaning: a fake bid placed to raise the price
items.example: Shill plus bid names the false offer made on behalf of the seller.
items.exampleCN: shill 与 bid 合成，指替卖家发出的虚假出价。

items.meaning: a person who bids for the seller
items.example: Bidder carries the agent sense of the person who does the act.
items.exampleCN: bidder 表示实施该动作的人。

items.example: The phrase names the practice of pushing prices with planted bids.
items.exampleCN: 这个短语指用安插的出价抬价的做法。

由本词与 bid 合成，义为抬价的假出价

definition_zh: 胫；小腿前部；胫骨（口语）；（手脚并用）攀爬
definition_en: the front part of the leg between the knee and the ankle, the bone just under its skin, or the action of climbing up something with hands and legs together
core_image: 膝盖到脚踝之间那条硬硬的、紧贴皮肤的骨棱
scene: 球场边，球员被绊了一下，抱着小腿前侧那块硬骨棱蹲在地上直吸气。The player grabbed his shin and could not stand up for a moment.
sceneCN: 这里 shin 是「胫、小腿前部」（第 1 个义项：膝盖到脚踝之间、紧贴皮肤的那段硬骨棱）；句意：球员抱住胫部，一时站不起来。那里的骨头几乎没有肉垫着，一撞就疼。

pos.zh: 胫；小腿前部；胫骨（口语）
手脚并用地攀爬（常与 up 连用）；踢（某人）的胫部

derivatives.zh: 由本词与 bone 合成，义为「胫骨」，即小腿前面那根粗骨
由本词加词尾构成，义为「攀爬」，与 shin up 同源同义，多见于北美英语
由本词与 guard 合成，义为「护胫；护腿」，足球与冰球运动员常戴
与本词同源但词义另走一路，义为「简易街头冰球」；与攀爬义的 shinny 拼写相同而来源不同

senses.title: The front of the lower leg
senses.definition: the front part of the leg between the knee and the ankle, where the bone lies just under the skin
senses.definitionCN: 膝盖与脚踝之间的小腿前部，那里的骨头几乎就贴着皮肤
senses.example: He banged his shin against the edge of the table and had to hop on one leg.
senses.exampleCN: 他的小腿撞到桌子角，疼得只好单脚跳。
senses.why: The Old English word named the leg bone, so the bone and the front of the leg that it shapes came to share one name.
senses.whyCN: 古英语这个词本指腿骨，于是骨头和它撑起的小腿前面就同用了一个名字。

senses.title: The bone under the skin
senses.definition: the main bone of the lower leg, which runs down the front and can be felt through the skin
senses.definitionCN: 小腿的主要长骨，顺着前面一路向下，隔着皮肤就能摸到
senses.example: The doctor said the shin was cracked but not fully broken.
senses.exampleCN: 医生说胫骨裂了，但还没有完全断。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense the word carried, because Old English scinu named the bone before it named the region around it.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个词最古老的含义：古英语 scinu 先指骨头，然后才指骨头周围的那片区域。

senses.title: To climb with arms and legs
senses.definition: to climb up a pole, a tree or a rope by gripping it with the arms and legs together, and by kicking the shins against it
senses.definitionCN: 双手抱住、双腿夹住杆子、树干或绳子，靠小腿抵着蹬上去
senses.example: She shinned up the drainpipe and reached the flat roof within a minute.
senses.exampleCN: 她手脚并用沿着排水管爬上去，不到一分钟就到了平屋顶。
senses.why: To climb without steps you press the shin hard against the surface, so the leg part gave its name to the whole action.
senses.whyCN: 没有梯子可踩时，人得用小腿死死抵住杆面往上蹭，于是这个身体部位的名字成了整个动作的名称。

senses.title: To kick someone on the shin
senses.definition: to hit a person hard and quickly on the shin, usually with the foot or the knee
senses.definitionCN: 用脚或膝盖又快又重地撞在别人的胫部
senses.example: The boy shinned his attacker where it hurt most.
senses.exampleCN: 男孩朝袭击者身上最疼的地方踢了一脚。
senses.why: If the shin is the weakest spot of a guard, then to shin someone is to aim for exactly that spot.
senses.whyCN: 如果胫部是防守中最脆弱的地方，那么 to shin someone 就是把攻击对准了那里。

senses.title: A fishplate on a railway
senses.definition: a flat bar of metal that joins two sections of railway rail end to end
senses.definitionCN: 把两段铁轨首尾接起来的扁平金属板
senses.example: A worker tightened the bolts on each shin where the rails met.
senses.exampleCN: 工人把铁轨接头处每块夹板上的螺栓都拧紧了。
senses.why: This technical sense comes from the supposed shape of the bone plate that the rail bar resembles, so it is a naming by resemblance rather than a new meaning of the body.
senses.whyCN: 这个技术义来自夹板形似腿骨所想到的那块板，所以它是按形似来命名，并不是身体义的新意思。

senses.title: The Hebrew letter shin
senses.definition: the twenty-first letter of the Hebrew alphabet, written to look like a crown with three upward points
senses.definitionCN: 希伯来字母表的第二十一个字母，形如带三个朝上尖角的王冠
senses.example: The letter shin stands at the head of several Hebrew prayers.
senses.exampleCN: 希伯来字母 shin 出现在好几段祷文的开头。
senses.why: This letter name belongs to the Semitic alphabet tradition with no link to the leg, so in a dictionary it must be kept as a separate headword.
senses.whyCN: 这个字母名属于闪米特字母传统，和腿没有关系，所以在词典里必须作为独立的词条看待。

intro.en: Shin goes back to Old English scinu, a word for the leg bone from which the front of the lower leg takes its name; its deeper Germanic and Indo-European roots are reconstructable but not recorded.
intro.cn: shin 可追溯至古英语 scinu，本指腿骨，小腿前面因此得名；更早的日耳曼语与印欧语词根属于可重构但无文献记录的形式。

items.en: A reconstructed root skei, meaning to cut or to split, is generally placed behind the Germanic words for shin and similar thin, flat parts.
items.cn: 一般认为，德语族中表示胫部以及类似薄而平的东西的词，背后可重构出一个意为「切、劈开」的词根 skei。

items.en: The reconstructed form skinwo, the leg bone, develops from that root; the form is a reconstruction and not a written record.
items.cn: 可重构出 skinwo，意为腿骨；这只是重构形式，并非文献记录。

items.en: Old English scinu names the shinbone and the lower leg, kept in the strong feminine declension.
items.cn: 古英语 scinu 指胫骨与小腿，属于强变化阴性名词。

items.en: The spelling settles as shin, and the word covers the front of the leg as well as the bone.
items.cn: 拼写固定为 shin，词义同时覆盖腿的前面与那块骨头。

items.en: The verb shin up, to climb by gripping with the shins, spreads in the nineteenth century, and shin splints enters use in the twentieth.
items.cn: shin up 这一表示「用小腿抵着往上爬」的动词用法在十九世纪流行开来，shin splints 则在二十世纪进入日常语言。

items.en: Modern English keeps the body sense, the climbing verb, the railway plate and the Hebrew letter name side by side.
items.cn: 现代英语同时保持着身体义、攀爬动词义、铁路夹板义与希伯来字母名。

note.en: Shin sits among the body part words of the lower leg and is easily confused in spelling with thin, shine and shinny.
note.cn: shin 属于小腿部位的词族，在拼写上又容易与 thin、shine 和 shinny 相混。

entries.definition: to give out or reflect light
entries.definitionCN: 发光；照耀；只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: narrow, or not thick
entries.definitionCN: 细的；薄的；只是拼写相近且元音近似，词源不同

entries.definition: to climb up something by gripping and pulling
entries.definitionCN: 攀爬；由本词加词尾构成，与 shin up 同义

entries.definition: the medical name for the shinbone
entries.definitionCN: 胫骨的医学正式名称

entries.definition: the thick fleshy back part of the lower leg
entries.definitionCN: 小腿肚；指小腿后面柔软的肌肉部分

entries.definition: the joint in the middle of the leg
entries.definitionCN: 膝盖；小腿与大腿相接的关节

normalIntro.en: Shin is an Old English bone word, so its body senses and its climbing verb both grow from the idea of pressing the leg against something hard.
normalIntro.cn: shin 是古英语的腿骨词，它的身体义和攀爬动词义都源自「用小腿死死抵住硬物」这个动作。

normal.en: Old English scinu named the leg bone first, so the front of the leg carries the bone name.
normal.cn: 古英语 scinu 先指腿骨，所以小腿前面一直带着的是骨头的名字。

normal.en: Shin up means to climb by gripping with hands and shins, as on a pole or a pipe.
normal.cn: shin up 指手脚并用、以小腿抵着爬上杆子或水管。

normal.en: Common partners: shin injury, shin pad, shin splints and shin-deep water.
normal.cn: 常用搭配：胫部损伤、护胫、胫骨劳损，以及水到小腿那么深。

normal.en: Shinbone is the everyday word for the bone that medics call the tibia.
normal.cn: 日常说 shinbone，就是医学上叫作 tibia 的那根骨头。

normal.en: Compare calf: the calf is the soft back of the lower leg, while the shin is the hard front.
normal.cn: 对比 calf：小腿肚在小腿后面、柔软；shin 在小腿前面、坚硬。

abstract.en: Picture a hand running down the front of a leg and stopping at a long ridge of bone.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手顺着腿的前面往下摸，摸到一条长长的硬骨棱。

abstract.en: Picture a child gripping a thin pole, the shins pressed flat against it, sliding up an arm length at a time.
abstract.cn: 想象一个孩子抱住细细的柱子，小腿紧贴柱面，一下一下往上蹿。

abstract.en: Picture a runner bent over and pressing both hands on the front of a leg after a hard race.
abstract.cn: 想象一名跑者跑完硬仗后弯下身，双手按在腿的前面。

examples.en: She banged her shin on the low gate and later found a dark bruise.
examples.cn: 她的小腿撞上了矮门，后来留下一块深色淤青。

examples.en: The thieves shinned up the wall and dropped into the garden.
examples.cn: 窃贼手脚并用翻上墙，落进了园子。

examples.en: Footballers wear shin pads to soften the blows from other players.
examples.cn: 足球运动员戴护胫，好减轻别人的撞击。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「新」——膝盖到脚踝之间那条又硬又新的骨棱，一撞就疼得记住；这只是谐音联想，与古英语 scinu 无关。

root: 古英语 scinu（腿骨；小腿）→ 中古英语 shin → 现代英语 shin；一般认为更早可重构出日耳曼语 skinwo 与印欧语词根 skei（切、劈开）。核心义是「膝盖到脚踝之间那条贴着皮肤的硬骨棱」。

sensesIntro.en: Shin begins as a bone word, then names the front of the lower leg, gives its name to a climbing action and a kick, and also to a railway bar that looks like the bone plate; the Hebrew letter is a separate homograph.
sensesIntro.cn: shin 起初是骨头词，后来指小腿前面，又把自己的名字给了攀爬动作与踢胫这一击，还给了形似骨板的铁路夹板；希伯来字母则是同形异源的另一个词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a long hard ridge of bone running from the knee down to the ankle, with only skin over it.
core.cn: 核心意象：从膝盖一路通到脚踝的一条长寿骨棱，上面只隔着一层皮。

branches.en: BODY LINE: the bone and the front of the leg it shapes.
branches.cn: 身体线：骨头本身，以及被它撑起的小腿前面。

branches.en: ACTION LINE: pressing the shin against a surface becomes the climbing verb.
branches.cn: 动作线：用小腿抵住表面往上蹭，变成了攀爬动词。

branches.en: HIT LINE: to strike the most exposed spot is to shin someone.
branches.cn: 打击线：对准最没有遮挡的地方打，就叫 shin someone。

branches.en: SHAPE LINE: a railway joining plate borrows the look of the bone plate.
branches.cn: 形状线：铁路接轨夹板借用了骨板的样子来命名。

branches.en: SEPARATE WORD: the Hebrew letter shares only the spelling.
branches.cn: 独立词条：希伯来字母名只与它共用拼写。

intro.en: Shin is an Old English whole word, and modern English builds its small family by compounding with bone, guard and pad, and by the ending -y in shinny.
intro.cn: shin 是古英语的整词，现代英语用与 bone、guard、pad 复合以及加词尾 -y 的办法种出它的小词族。

latinIntro.en: The word is Germanic rather than Latin, so there are no Latin cognates here; the stem behind it is a reconstruction.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词属于日耳曼语而非拉丁语，因此这里没有拉丁同源词；它背后的词干属于重构形式。

items.meaning: the front of the lower leg
items.example: Shin keeps the Old English bone word as a single unit.
items.exampleCN: shin 把古英语的腿骨词整套保留为一个单元。

items.example: Old English scinu is the recorded ancestor of the word.
items.exampleCN: 古英语 scinu 是这个词有文献可查的祖形。

items.meaning: more than one; third person singular
items.example: The ending -s forms shins for both the noun and the verb.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -s 既构成名词复数 shins，也构成动词三单 shins。

items.example: The ending -ed forms shinned, with the final n doubled.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ed 构成 shinned，末尾的 n 要双写。

items.example: The ending -ing forms shinning, with the n doubled as well.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 构成 shinning，末尾的 n 同样要双写。

items.meaning: the main bone of the lower leg
items.example: Shin plus bone makes the everyday name of the tibia.
items.exampleCN: shin 与 bone 合成，就是胫骨的日常叫法。

items.meaning: a pad worn over the shin
items.example: Guard shows what the pad is for, protection of the shin.
items.exampleCN: guard 点出这个护具的作用，即保护胫部。

items.meaning: forming a related verb or adjective
items.meaningCN: 构成相关动词或形容词的词尾
items.example: The suffix -y forms shinny, another word for climbing.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -y 构成 shinny，是表示攀爬的另一个说法。

items.example: Skinwo or skinwa, both written as reconstructions, is the usual Proto-Germanic form.
items.exampleCN: skinwo 或 skinwa 都写作重构形式，是通常给出的原始日耳曼语形式。

items.meaning: to climb by gripping and pulling
items.example: Shinny is the North American partner of shin up.
items.exampleCN: shinny 是北美英语里与 shin up 对应的说法。

derivatives.zh: 由本词与 bone 合成，义为「胫骨」
由本词加词尾构成，义为「攀爬」
由本词与 guard 合成，义为「护胫」

definition_zh: 岸；海滨；湖滨；支撑；支持；撑住
definition_en: the land along the edge of a sea, lake, or other large body of water, or to prop something up and keep it steady
core_image: 陆地与水面相接的一条边，人站在边缘上
scene: 退潮以后，孩子们在岸边捡拾贝壳。After the tide went out, the children hunted for shells along the shore.
sceneCN: 这里 shore 是「海岸、岸边」（第 1 个义项：水边的大片陆地）；句意：退潮以后，孩子们在岸边捡拾贝壳。

pos.zh: 岸；海滨；湖滨；岸坡
支撑；撑住；使稳住

collocations.zh: 从一岸到另一岸；遍及各地

derivatives.zh: 由基础词加 line 构成，义为「海岸线」
由基础词加 off 构成，义为「离岸的；向海的」
由基础词加 on 构成，义为「在岸上的；向岸的」
由 sea 加基础词构成，义为「海滨；海岸」
由基础词加 ing 构成，义为「支撑物；撑架」

senses.title: Land along a large body of water
senses.definition: the land that runs along the edge of a sea, lake, or wide river
senses.definitionCN: 沿海洋、湖泊或宽阔河流边缘延伸的陆地
senses.example: We walked along the shore in the evening.
senses.exampleCN: 傍晚我们沿着海岸散步。
senses.why: The word began as an edge or boundary, and the sea edge became the picture people kept.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初表示「边缘、分界」，水面的边缘成了人们保留至今的画面。

senses.title: The seaside region
senses.definition: a coastal area or place by the sea, often used in names
senses.definitionCN: 靠海的一带地区或城镇，常用于地名
senses.example: They rented a cottage on the shore for the summer.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在海滨租了一间小屋过夏天。
senses.why: From a thin line along the water, the sense stretched to the whole band of land nearby.
senses.whyCN: 从水边的一条细线，词义扩展为附近的一整片陆地。

senses.title: Safely on land
senses.definition: on or towards land, away from deep water, as in ashore
senses.definitionCN: 在陆地上或向陆地靠拢，离开深水，如 ashore 所示
senses.example: After three weeks at sea, the sailors were glad to reach the shore.
senses.exampleCN: 在海上漂了三周以后，船员们很高兴能上岸。
senses.why: For sailors the shore is the exact line where danger stops and dry ground begins.
senses.whyCN: 对水手而言，岸正是危险结束、干燥陆地开始的那条界线。

senses.title: The bank of an inland waterway
senses.definition: the bank of a lake or wide river, where the land meets the still or flowing water
senses.definitionCN: 湖泊或宽阔河流的岸，陆地与静水或流水相接之处
senses.example: Fishermen sat on the far shore of the lake.
senses.exampleCN: 渔民们坐在湖的对岸。
senses.why: Very few coastal features are truly specific, and the same edge image fits rivers and lakes.
senses.whyCN: 「岸」这个边缘意象本就不限于海洋，同样适用于江河与湖泊。

senses.title: To prop something up
senses.definition: to support a weak structure with a pole or beam so that it stays upright
senses.definitionCN: 用柱子或横木撑住不牢固的结构，使其保持直立
senses.example: Workers shored up the old wall with thick beams.
senses.exampleCN: 工人们用粗木梁撑住了那面老墙。
senses.why: A prop stands at the edge of a falling thing, holding it like a shore holds back the water.
senses.whyCN: 支撑物立在将倒之物的边缘，像岸抵御水一样把它撑住。

senses.title: To strengthen something abstract
senses.definition: to support or strengthen a business, system, or belief, especially one that is failing
senses.definitionCN: 支撑或加强陷入困境的生意、体系或信念
senses.example: The government shored up the bank with public money.
senses.exampleCN: 政府用公共资金支撑这家银行。
senses.why: Money lent to a failing firm works exactly like a beam under a cracked wall.
senses.whyCN: 借给濒危公司的资金，作用就像撑在裂墙下的木梁。

intro.en: Shore as a coast stands apart from shore meaning a prop, and the two words are thought to come from different roots.
intro.cn: 表示「岸」的 shore 与表示「支撑物」的 shore 被认为不同源，前者是海岸词，后者是支撑词。

items.en: Scora means a shore or coast, with related forms in the sea edge sense.
items.cn: 古英语 scora 意为岸、海岸，并有一组相应的同源形式。

items.en: Scieran means to cut or divide, which fits the image of land cut off by water.
items.cn: 古英语 scieran 意为切割、分开，正合「被水隔开的陆地」这一画面。

items.en: Schore names the sea edge, and the word also spreads to the banks of lakes.
items.cn: 中古英语 schore 指海边的边缘，词义也扩展到湖泊的岸。

items.en: Shore becomes the standard written form for a coast, while the verb shore comes from a separate prop word.
items.cn: 现代英语把 shore 固定为表示「海岸」的写法，而动词「支撑」来自另一个表示支柱的词。

items.en: The phrasal verb shore up spreads from building work to finance and politics.
items.cn: 短语动词 shore up 从建筑施工扩展到金融与政治领域。

note.en: Shore is close to its water-edge family in form and to other coast words in meaning.
note.cn: shore 在形式上靠近它的「水边」词族，在意义上靠近其他表示海岸的词。

entries.definition: the line where land meets water
entries.definitionCN: 海岸线

entries.definition: on or towards the land from the sea
entries.definitionCN: 在岸上；向岸上

entries.definition: past participle of shear, cut off
entries.definitionCN: shear 的过去分词，意为「被剪去的」；只是拼写相近，词源与 shore 不同

entries.definition: the land beside the sea or ocean
entries.definitionCN: 海岸；沿海地区

entries.definition: an area of sand or stones beside the sea
entries.definitionCN: 沙滩；海滩

entries.definition: the land along each side of a river
entries.definitionCN: 河岸；河堤

normalIntro.en: Shore is the edge where dry land stops and water starts.
normalIntro.cn: shore 就是干燥陆地停住、水面开始的那条边。

normal.en: On the shore means standing where the water meets the land.
normal.cn: on the shore 表示站在水陆交界处。

normal.en: Shore up a wall means put a beam under it to hold it.
normal.cn: shore up a wall 表示在墙下撑一根梁把它顶住。

normal.en: Shoreline adds line and names the exact edge.
normal.cn: shoreline 加上 line，指那条精确的边线。

normal.en: Ashore means away from the water and onto dry land.
normal.cn: ashore 表示离开水面，登上陆地。

normal.en: Compare beach: beach is the sand, shore is the whole edge.
normal.cn: 对比 beach：beach 指沙子，shore 指整条水边。

abstract.en: Picture a thin ribbon of sand separating sea and field.
abstract.cn: 想象一条细沙带把海和田野分隔开。

abstract.en: Think of a ship turning from deep water towards the lights of land.
abstract.cn: 想象一艘船从深水掉头，朝岸上的灯光驶去。

abstract.en: Imagine a wooden post leaning against a tired old wall.
abstract.cn: 想象一根木柱斜撑在一堵摇摇欲坠的旧墙上。

examples.en: She sat on the shore watching the boats come in.
examples.cn: 她坐在岸边看渔船进港。

examples.en: Engineers shored up the bridge after the flood.
examples.cn: 洪水过后，工程师们加固了那座桥。

examples.en: The lake shore is lined with pine trees.
examples.cn: 湖岸边种满了松树。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「笑」——海岸边风大，人迎着风笑，就想到 shore；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 scora（岸、海岸），可能与「切割」义的 scieran 有关，指被水面切开的陆地边缘；表示「支撑」的动词来源不同。

sensesIntro.en: Shore starts as the edge of water, widens to the seaside region, then to the land sailors reach, and finally turns into the act of holding something up.
sensesIntro.cn: shore 从水面的边缘出发，先扩展为整片海滨地区与船员登陆的陆地，最后转为「撑住某物」的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a strip of land pressed against the water.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条陆地被水紧紧压着。

branches.en: The edge of a sea or lake is the central sense.
branches.cn: 海洋或湖泊的边缘是核心义项。

branches.en: The seaside region stretches the edge into a whole area.
branches.cn: 海滨地区把一条边扩展成一整片区域。

branches.en: Reaching the shore means reaching safety on land.
branches.cn: 抵达岸边就意味着到达了陆地上的安全处。

branches.en: Sea shore and lake shore share the same meeting of land and water.
branches.cn: 海与湖的岸共享同一个水陆相接的画面。

branches.en: Propping a wall and propping a bank both hold up something falling.
branches.cn: 撑住墙与支撑银行都是把将倒之物顶住。

intro.en: Shore joins with short words like sea line on and off, and the verb has its own prop word.
intro.cn: shore 与 sea、line、on、off 等短词组合成新词，动词「支撑」另有独立的来源。

latinIntro.en: Shore is a native English word, and its Latin entries are only the distant cut root behind it.
latinIntro.cn: shore 是本族英语词，其在拉丁语中的对应只是词根层面「切割」义的远亲。

items.example: Shore is the base noun.
items.exampleCN: shore 是基础名词。

items.example: The suffix -line forms shoreline.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -line 构成 shoreline。

items.example: The suffix -less forms shoreless.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -less 构成 shoreless。

items.exampleCN: 前缀 off- 构成 offshore。

items.example: Shore up is used for walls and finances.
items.exampleCN: shore up 常用于墙体和资金。

items.example: Shoring names the props themselves.
items.exampleCN: shoring 指支撑物本身。

definition_zh: 速记；速记法；简略表达；简称
definition_en: a quick system of writing in which symbols stand for words or sounds, or a short and informal way of saying something
core_image: 手写得飞快，一个符号顶替一整个词
scene: 会议速度很快，她靠速记记下了每句话的重点。The speaker was fast, so she used shorthand to capture the main points.
sceneCN: 这里 shorthand 是「速记法」（第 1 个义项：用符号快速记录说话的书写法）；句意：会议速度很快，她靠速记记下了每句话的重点。

pos.zh: 速记；速记法；简洁的表述；简称
速记的；简写的

derivatives.zh: 组合中的第二部分，义为「手；手写」，指书写方式
组合的第一部分，义为「短的」，指书写省时简短
与基础词相对的后造词，义为「普通书写；非速记的写法」

senses.title: A fast system of writing
senses.definition: a system of rapid writing that uses symbols or shortened letters for words and sounds
senses.definitionCN: 用符号或缩略字母代替词和音的快速书写系统
senses.example: The clerk took the interview down in shorthand.
senses.exampleCN: 书记员用速记记下了这次采访。
senses.why: Short plus hand names a hand that writes in a short way, so speed is built into the word.
senses.whyCN: short 加 hand 指「写得短的手」，速度从构词之初就包含在里面。

senses.title: A short way of expressing things
senses.definition: a short and informal word or symbol used instead of a longer name or idea
senses.definitionCN: 用来代替较长名称或概念的简短通俗说法或符号
senses.example: Wall Street is often shorthand for the whole finance industry.
senses.exampleCN: 华尔街常被用作整个金融业的代称。
senses.why: If symbols can stand for whole words on paper, a short label can stand for a big idea in speech too.
senses.whyCN: 既然符号能在纸上代替整个词，一个短标签在口语里也能代替一整套概念。

senses.title: The quality of being concise
senses.definition: the character of language that is scaled down yet still clear
senses.definitionCN: 语言被压缩却依然清楚的特点
senses.example: The novel has a shorthand kind of precision.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说有一种简练而精确的风格。
senses.why: When writing is pressed into a few marks, the value of being brief starts to stand on its own.
senses.whyCN: 当书写被压成寥寥几笔，「简练」本身就成了一种独立的价值。

senses.title: A private code shared by a group
senses.definition: a set of signs or words that only a particular group understands
senses.definitionCN: 只有某个特定群体才懂得的一组符号或说法
senses.example: Journalists share a shorthand their readers never see.
senses.exampleCN: 记者们有一套读者从未见过的圈内门道。
senses.why: Rapid notes are useful only if the writer knows the signs, and this shared knowledge becomes group identity.
senses.whyCN: 快速记下的符号只对认得的人有用，这种共同知识于是变成了群体身份。

senses.title: Something that stands for something else
senses.definition: a symbol or sign that stands for an idea, place, or feeling in a few marks
senses.definitionCN: 用很少几笔代表某种理念、地点或情感的符号或标志
senses.example: The red umbrella became shorthand for the charity.
senses.exampleCN: 这把红伞成了那家慈善机构的标志。
senses.why: The same principle that lets one stroke carry a word lets one object carry a whole institution.
senses.whyCN: 一笔能顶一个词的道理，同样能让一个物件顶替一整个机构。

intro.en: Shorthand is a compound of short and hand, naming a style of writing done by hand in a short way.
intro.cn: shorthand 由 short 与 hand 复合而成，指用手做得短而快的书写方式。

items.en: Scort means short and comes from the same root as Modern English short.
items.cn: 古英语 scort 意为短的，与现代英语 short 同出一源。

items.en: Isaac Pitman publishes a system of fast writing and gives it the name shorthand.
items.cn: 伊萨克·皮特曼发表了一套快速书写法，并用 shorthand 为它命名。

items.en: Shorthand becomes the standard term for writing done with symbols instead of full words.
items.cn: 19 世纪 shorthand 成为以符号代替完整单词的书写法的标准名称。

items.en: The word spreads beyond offices and comes to mean a brief way of saying anything.
items.cn: 这个词走出办公室，用来指对任何事物的简略表达。

items.en: Shorthand is now a common metaphor for a symbol standing for a larger idea.
items.cn: 20 世纪起 shorthand 常作隐喻，指代表更大概念的象征。

note.en: Shorthand is near its shortened-writing family in form and near brief expression words in meaning.
note.cn: shorthand 在形式上靠近「缩短书写」的词族，在意义上靠近表示「简明表达」的词。

entries.definition: ordinary writing with full letters
entries.definitionCN: 用完整字母的普通书写

entries.definition: to write by hand
entries.definitionCN: 手写

entries.definition: a quicker way to do something
entries.definitionCN: 捷径；快捷方式

entries.definition: a shortened form of a word
entries.definitionCN: 缩写；缩略形式

entries.definition: the formal art of writing in shorthand
entries.definitionCN: 速记术（正式说法）

entries.definition: a brief account of the main points
entries.definitionCN: 摘要；概要

normalIntro.en: Shorthand says its own design: short plus hand, writing done quickly by hand.
normalIntro.cn: shorthand 本身就是构造说明：short 加 hand，用手写得短而快。

normal.en: Shorthand for means a short name standing for something bigger.
normal.cn: shorthand for 表示代替更大事物的简称。

normal.en: In shorthand means notes written with symbols.
normal.cn: in shorthand 表示用符号记下的笔记。

normal.en: A shorthand typist took the letters at speed.
normal.cn: shorthand typist 指会速记的打字员，能以极快的速度打出信件。

normal.en: Longhand contrasts with shorthand: full letters, slower pace.
normal.cn: longhand 与 shorthand 相对：用完整字母，速度更慢。

normal.en: Compare abbreviation: an abbreviation shortens words, shorthand writes whole speech quickly.
normal.cn: 对比 abbreviation：缩写缩短单词，速记则快速记下整段话。

abstract.en: Picture a pen racing across a page in curls and hooks.
abstract.cn: 想象一支笔在纸上以弯钩和圈圈飞快划过。

abstract.en: Think of one dollar sign replacing a sentence about money.
abstract.cn: 想象一个美元符号代替了关于钱的一整句话。

abstract.en: Imagine a single red umbrella that everyone links to one charity.
abstract.cn: 想象一把红伞，所有人都把它和同一家慈善机构联系起来。

examples.en: She learned shorthand to keep up with the court hearing.
examples.cn: 她学了速记，以跟上庭审的语速。

examples.en: The word shop is shorthand for the whole project team.
examples.cn: 这句里的 shop 是整个项目组的简称。

examples.en: His letters were written in shorthand and hard to read.
examples.cn: 他的信是用速记写的，很难辨认。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「少含」——速记就是少含内容、写得飞快；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 英语本土复合词，short（短的）加 hand（手、手写的字迹），字面义「短的手写」，指写得短而快的书写法，后引申为「简略表达、象征」。

sensesIntro.en: Shorthand begins as a fast writing system, widens to any brief label, then to concision itself, and finally to shared codes and standing symbols.
sensesIntro.cn: shorthand 先指快速书写的方法，再扩展为任何简短的代称，进而指简练本身，最后引申为圈内暗语与象征符号。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand racing across paper, one mark for a whole word.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手在纸上飞写，一个记号顶一个词。

branches.en: Symbol writing for speed is the first and literal sense.
branches.cn: 为求速度而用符号书写，是最初的字面义项。

branches.en: A short name for a big idea grows from the same compression.
branches.cn: 用短名称指代大概念，源于同样的压缩逻辑。

branches.en: Concision becomes a style quality, not only a method.
branches.cn: 简练从一种方法变成一种风格特征。

branches.en: Fast notes only work for those who know the shared signs.
branches.cn: 快速笔记只对认得共同符号的人有用。

branches.en: A shorthand and a symbol both let one small thing stand for a big one.
branches.cn: 简称与象征都让一件小东西代表一个大事物。

intro.en: Shorthand is a warm English compound, and its parts short and hand also build longhand and handwrite.
intro.cn: shorthand 是英语本土复合词，其构词部件 short 与 hand 也构成 longhand、handwrite 等词。

latinIntro.en: Shorthand has no Latin family of its own, so its Latin entries list only the idea of writing with symbols.
latinIntro.cn: shorthand 本身没有拉丁词族，这里的拉丁条目只列出表示「书写、速记」的单词供对照。

items.example: Shore is only a spelling neighbour.
items.exampleCN: shore 只是拼写上的近邻。

items.example: Short is the first element of the compound.
items.exampleCN: short 是复合词的第一部件。

items.example: Hand is the second element of the compound.
items.exampleCN: hand 是复合词的第二部件。

items.example: Longhand was coined against shorthand.
items.exampleCN: longhand 是为与 shorthand 相对而造的。

items.example: Handwrite shares the hand element.
