definition_zh: 精品；代表作；展品；招牌项目
definition_en: an excellent object or project shown to impress people as the best example of what a place or group can do
core_image: 展台上被聚光灯照亮、供人赞叹的那一件
scene: 博物馆把最精美的瓷瓶放在大厅中央，作为镇馆之宝。The museum placed its finest vase in the entrance hall as the showpiece of the collection.
sceneCN: 这里 showpiece 是「精品、镇馆之宝」（第 1 个义项：展示出来镇场面的最佳物件）；句意：博物馆把最精美的瓷瓶放在大厅中央，作为镇馆之宝。

pos.zh: 精品；代表作；展品；招牌项目

derivatives.zh: 组合的第一部分，义为「展示；展览」，指公开展出让人们看
组合的第二部分，义为「一件、一件作品」，指单个物件

senses.title: The finest object on display
senses.definition: an object kept and displayed because it is the best of its kind
senses.definitionCN: 因同类中最佳而被保存并展出的物件
senses.example: The diamond necklace was the showpiece of the exhibition.
senses.exampleCN: 那条钻石项链是整场展览的精品。
senses.why: Show plus piece literally means a piece set out to be shown, so the word starts with a displayed item.
senses.whyCN: show 加 piece 字面上就是「拿出来展示的一件」，所以词义一开始就是被展出的物件。

senses.title: A place or building worth seeing
senses.definition: a building, town, or public place looked after and admired as its best feature
senses.definitionCN: 被用心维护、作为最大亮点而受人赞赏的建筑、城镇或公共场所
senses.example: The new library is the showpiece of the town.
senses.exampleCN: 新图书馆是这座小镇的招牌建筑。
senses.why: Buildings are shown off in the same way as objects, so the sense widens from a thing to a place.
senses.whyCN: 建筑和物件一样会被拿出来炫耀，所以词义从一件东西扩展到一处地方。

senses.title: A project or event presented as a success
senses.definition: a project or event that people present proudly as proof of success
senses.definitionCN: 人们自豪地展示、用以证明成功的项目或活动
senses.example: The festival became a showpiece for the region.
senses.exampleCN: 这个节庆成了该地区的招牌活动。
senses.why: Once a stage can be a showpiece, any planned effort put on display takes on the same role.
senses.whyCN: 一旦场地能成为精品，任何被摆出来让人看的策划成果也能扮演同样的角色。

senses.title: Someone treated as a display of success
senses.titleCN: 被当作摆样的人；招牌人物
senses.definition: a person who is valued mainly as evidence of a group or success
senses.definitionCN: 主要因其代表某个群体或成就而被看重的人
senses.example: The young champion was hurried out as a showpiece for the sponsors.
senses.exampleCN: 那位年轻冠军被匆匆推出来，为赞助商做宣传招牌。
senses.why: If a good object can be turned into a display, so can a talented person, though the tone turns somewhat critical.
senses.whyCN: 好物件能被做成展品，有才华的人也会被推出来展示，只是语气带上了几分批评意味。

senses.title: The chief ornament of an occasion
senses.definition: the most impressive item in a collection or programme, the one kept for the end
senses.definitionCN: 一组收藏或一个节目单中最精彩、留到最后出场的那一项
senses.example: The fireworks were the showpiece of the evening.
senses.exampleCN: 烟花是那个夜晚的压轴亮点。
senses.why: In an evening order the best is usually saved for the climax, and that single item earns the name.
senses.whyCN: 在晚会的次序里，最好的常留作高潮，那一项便得了这个名称。

intro.en: Showpiece is a plain English compound, show plus piece, coined for the object displayed as the best.
intro.cn: showpiece 是直白的英语复合词，show 加 piece，为「展示出来的最佳物件」而造。

items.en: Scawian means to look at or show, and Modern English show keeps this sense.
items.cn: 古英语 scawian 意为观看、展示，现代英语 show 保留了这层意思。

items.en: Piece comes through Old French from a Latin word for a part or portion.
items.cn: piece 经古法语而来，源头是拉丁语中表示「部分、一块」的词。

items.en: Showpiece appears as a compound name for the best item put on display.
items.cn: 19 世纪出现复合词 showpiece，用来称呼展示出来的最佳物件。

items.en: The word spreads from stage costumes to public buildings, therefore its sense widens.
items.cn: 这个词从舞台服装扩展到公共建筑，因而词义明显扩展。

items.en: Showpiece is used for flagship projects and events in business and politics.
items.cn: 20 世纪起 showpiece 用于商业与政治中的旗舰项目与重大活动。

note.en: Showpiece is close to show compounds in form and to words for best examples in meaning.
note.cn: showpiece 在形式上靠近由 show 构成的复合词，在意义上靠近表示「最佳范例」的词。

normalIntro.en: Showpiece reads as it stands: the piece you show to everyone.
normalIntro.cn: showpiece 顾名思义，就是拿出来给大家看的那一件。

normal.en: The showpiece of a collection is the item every visitor stops for.
normal.cn: showpiece of a collection 指每位参观者都会驻足的那件展品。

normal.en: A showpiece attraction draws the biggest crowd.
normal.cn: showpiece attraction 指吸引最多人的王牌景点。

normal.en: An architectural showpiece is a building people come to admire.
normal.cn: architectural showpiece 指专程来欣赏的建筑精品。

normal.en: Showroom and showcase share the showing idea with showpiece.
normal.cn: showroom 与 showcase 和 showpiece 共用「展示」这一想法。

normal.en: Compare masterpiece: a masterpiece is judged by skill, a showpiece by display.
normal.cn: 对比 masterpiece：masterpiece 看技艺高低，showpiece 看展示效果。

abstract.en: Picture a single vase lit by one bright lamp on a dark stage.
abstract.cn: 想象昏暗展台上，一盏灯独照着那只瓷瓶。

abstract.en: Think of a renovated station everyone is taken to see.
abstract.cn: 想象一座翻新后的车站，人人都被带去看看。

abstract.en: Imagine a champion carried forward at the end of the parade.
abstract.cn: 想象游行最后，一位冠军被众人拥到队伍最前面。

examples.en: The city rebuilt its riverfront as a showpiece for visitors.
examples.cn: 这座城市把河岸一带重建为向游客展示的招牌景观。

examples.en: The stadium was the showpiece of the games.
examples.cn: 这座体育场是那届运动会的标志性建筑。

examples.en: Critics said the young singer had become a showpiece for the label.
examples.cn: 评论家说那位年轻歌手已成了唱片公司的宣传招牌。

sensesIntro.cn: showpiece 先指被展示的最佳物件，再扩展到建筑与场所，进而指项目与活动，最后指被当成展示品的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one object under a spotlight, shown as the best.

branches.en: The finest displayed object is the literal sense.
branches.cn: 被展出的最佳物件是字面义项。

branches.en: A building or place becomes the item shown to guests.

branches.en: A project or event becomes proof of success on a stage.
branches.cn: 项目或活动成为舞台上证明成功的展品。

branches.en: People put on display and the climax of an evening both carry the display idea.

branches.en: A vase and a festival are both the one item a group wants others to see.
branches.cn: 瓷瓶与节庆都是群体希望别人看到的那一件。

definition_zh: 精明的；机敏的；敏锐的；狡猾的
definition_en: good at judging situations and people quickly, so that your decisions serve your own interest; sharp and practical rather than merely clever
core_image: 一双眼睛眯起来，快速算清对方的底牌和自己的筹码
scene: 老商人坐在客栈角落，听对方说了三句话，就看出这桩生意里哪里埋着亏空。He was too shrewd to sign the contract before he had read the small print.
sceneCN: 这里 shrewd 是「精明的、善于判断的」（第 1 个义项：判断形势与人物又快又准）；句意：他太精明了，不会没读完合同细则就签字。画面可想象：客栈角落、掌柜的算盘、一叠合同纸。

pos.zh: 精明的；机敏的；敏锐的；狡猾的
名词（罕见）：少数词典收作「精明的人」，现代英语几乎不用

derivatives.zh: 由本词加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「精明地；机敏地」
由本词加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「精明；机敏」
由本词加后缀 -ish 构成，义为「颇有几分精明的」，较少见

senses.title: Quick and accurate in judgement
senses.definition: able to understand a situation quickly and judge correctly what to do, especially when money or advantage is involved
senses.definitionCN: 能迅速看清形势并正确判断该怎么做，尤指在涉及钱财或利益时
senses.example: A shrewd investor sold her shares before the market fell.
senses.exampleCN: 一位精明的投资者在市场下跌前卖掉了股票。
senses.why: The oldest meaning of the word is malicious or cunning. Over the centuries it shifted from the sly cunning of the old noun shrewd to the practical cleverness of a person who reads a situation fast.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最早的意思是「恶毒的、狡猾的」；几百年里，它从原名词 shrewd 的「奸诈」慢慢转成了「看人看事一眼就准」的实用聪明。

senses.title: Sharp in noticing detail
senses.definition: showing sharp perception in noticing hidden motives, small details, or facts that others miss
senses.definitionCN: 在察觉隐藏动机、细枝末节或别人忽略的事实时表现出敏锐
senses.example: She gave the lawyer a shrewd look and said nothing.
senses.exampleCN: 她敏锐地看了律师一眼，什么也没说。
senses.why: Once the cunning becomes a quality of insight rather than of cheating, it attaches naturally to eyes and looks: the person who sees through the surface is shrewd.
senses.whyCN: 当「狡猾」不再指骗人而变成洞察力，它就自然附着在眼神上：能看穿表面的人就是 shrewd。

senses.title: Cunning, in diplomatic terms
senses.definition: clever in a calculating way, sometimes at the expense of fairness or plain dealing, though milder than calling someone devious
senses.definitionCN: 在打小算盘的意义上聪明，有时以牺牲公平或坦率为代价，但语气比 devious 温和
senses.example: The mayor was a shrewd operator who owed favours to no one.
senses.exampleCN: 这位市长精于政治运作，从不欠任何人的情。
senses.why: The modern adjective keeps one thread of the old malicious sense: a shrewd person is not cruel, but their cleverness is aimed at winning, and smart people sometimes dodge the rules.
senses.whyCN: 现代形容词保留了旧义的一丝线索：shrewd 的人并不残忍，但聪明是用在「赢」上，太聪明的人有时会绕开规则。

senses.title: A sharp comment
senses.definition: describing a remark or question that is pointed, hard to answer, and goes straight to the weak spot
senses.definitionCN: 形容言语或问题一针见血、难以回答，直指薄弱之处
senses.example: One shrewd question exposed the flaw in his argument.
senses.exampleCN: 一个一针见血的问题揭穿了他论证的漏洞。
senses.why: Judgement can be applied to words as well as to people: a remark that judges a situation accurately cuts as sharply as a blade.
senses.whyCN: 判断力既用在人身上，也用在话语上：准确判断形势的一句话，锋利得像刀刃。

intro.en: Shrewd began as an adjective of the noun shrew and took its modern sense of practical cleverness only in the sixteenth century.
intro.cn: shrewd 起初是由名词 shrew 派生的形容词，到十六世纪才获得现代「精明」的含义。

items.en: Scholar suggest *skrewwa or similar, and Old English had the related noun screawa, a name given to the shrew-mouse. Various small creatures cause similar mischief, so the exact identification of the animal is not certain.
items.cn: 学者推测原始形式近于 *skrewwa；古英语有相关名词 screawa，用来称呼尖鼠一类的小兽。多种小动物都可能招致类似的祸害，因此这只动物究竟指哪种，并不确定。

items.en: Shrew, the noun, also came to name a bad-tempered or abusive person, especially a woman with a sharp tongue. The origin of this metaphorical jump is uncertain.
items.cn: 名词 shrew 也用来指脾气暴躁或出口伤人的人，多指口舌锋利的女人。这一比喻义的来源不确定。

items.en: The derived adjective shrew was formed, meaning malicious, wicked or evil-natured; rude follows the same old pattern of turning a noun into an adjective.
items.cn: 由此派生的形容词 shrew 出现，意为「恶毒的、阴险的」；rude 这类词也走过同样的「名词变形容词」旧路。

items.en: Shrewd first appears with the sense malicious. During the sixteenth century it drifted to sharp-witted and astute, and the older senses faded.
items.cn: shrewd 最早出现的义项是「恶毒的」。十六世纪它逐渐变成「头脑敏锐、精明」，旧义随之淡出。

items.en: The animal name stays with the small mammal while the adjective is now used of merchants, investors and observers. The separate spellings are part of modern convention rather than of original form.
items.cn: 表示动物的小词仍指那种小型哺乳动物，而形容词如今多用于商人、投资者与观察者。两种拼写是后世约定俗成，并非原始形式之别。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words that sound or look like the same old root; the near-meaning group gathers cleverness words that differ in moral tone and in how openly the cleverness is used.
note.cn: 形近组收发音或拼写与旧词根相关的词；近义组收表示「聪明」的词，区别在于道德色彩以及聪明是否摆在明面上。

entries.definition: a small mammal with a long pointed snout, or, old-fashioned and insulting, a bad-tempered woman with a sharp tongue.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指吻部细长的小型哺乳动物；旧时也指脾气暴躁、口舌锋利的女人，属贬称。它是 shrewd 的派生基础。

entries.definition: bad-tempered and scolding, used mainly of women and now considered dated.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「脾气坏、爱骂人的」，多用于女性，如今已过时。与本词同源，但不表示「精明」。

entries.definition: The quality of being shrewd, formed directly from the adjective with the suffix -ness.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「精明、机敏」，由形容词直接加后缀 -ness 构成。

entries.definition: clever at seeing how a situation can be turned to advantage; closer to shrewd in English itself.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「精明的、敏锐的」，指能看出形势如何为己所用，与 shrewd 最接近，语气更书面。

entries.definition: clever in a secretive or deceitful way; much more negative than shrewd.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「狡猾的」，指暗中用计的聪明，贬义比 shrewd 重得多。

entries.definition: wise and showing deep judgement, more reflective and less self-serving than shrewd.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「睿智的」，强调深思熟虑的判断，比 shrewd 更端庄、更少自我盘算，属正式书面语。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real history of the word and the phrases it actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用这个词的真实历史，以及它实际出现的常见搭配。

normal.en: Shrewd comes from the noun shrew, the sharp-nosed animal that was once thought to bite and to curse.
normal.cn: shrewd 由名词 shrew 派生，那种尖嘴小兽旧时被认为会咬人、会招祸。

normal.en: In the sixteenth century the sense moved from malicious to sharp-witted; the sharpness stayed, the cruelty went.
normal.cn: 十六世纪义项从「恶毒」转向「机敏」：锋利留下了，残忍消失了。

normal.en: A shrewd businessman reads the other side before signing anything.
normal.cn: 精明的生意人签字前先把对方看透。

normal.en: Compare astute: astute is the book word, shrewd is the everyday one with a hint of self-interest.
normal.cn: 对比 astute：astute 偏书面，shrewd 更日常，还带一点「为自己打算」的意味。

normal.en: Compare cunning: cunning hides its tricks, shrewd just sees the situation clearly.
normal.cn: 对比 cunning：cunning 把手段藏起来，shrewd 只是把形势看得清楚。

abstract.en: Picture a pair of sharp eyes narrowing at a merchant table.
abstract.cn: 想象商桌旁一双眼睛眯成一条缝，眼神锋利。

abstract.en: Think of an eye that catches the one flaw in a page of small print.
abstract.cn: 想象一只眼睛在满页细则里一眼抓到那一处漏洞。

abstract.en: Imagine a chess player who knows which piece the opponent is about to move.
abstract.cn: 想象一位棋手，清楚对手下一步要动哪颗棋子。

examples.en: Her father was a shrewd shopkeeper who never bought stock at the wrong price.
examples.cn: 她的父亲是个精明的店主，从不在错误的价钱上进货。

examples.en: The critic made a shrewd guess about why the novel sold so well.
examples.cn: 评论家对这部小说为何畅销做出了一个敏锐的猜测。

examples.en: A shrewd negotiator noticed the nervous pause before the offer.
examples.cn: 一位精明的谈判者注意到了报价前那一阵紧张的停顿。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「数卢」——把账目数得一清二楚，人就显得精明；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 screawa 指一种小型尖嘴兽（一般认为即 shrew 鼠），来源不确定；名词 shrew 后引申为「恶人、泼妇」，形容词 shrewd 先意为「恶毒」，十六世纪转为「精明」。注意 shrew 鼠与 shrew 泼妇的拼写一致，但一个是动物，一个是隐喻。

sensesIntro.en: Shrewd always means the mind judges fast; the four senses differ in what is judged: a business or situation, a person and their motives, a political game, or the wording of a remark.
sensesIntro.cn: shrewd 始终表示头脑判断得快；四个义项的区别在于判断的对象：生意与形势、人与其动机、政治博弈，还是一句话的措辞。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pair of narrowing eyes reading a table of numbers or a face across the table.
core.cn: 核心意象：一双眯起的眼睛，读着桌上的数字或对面那张脸。

branches.en: THE DECISION: quick judgement about what to do with money or advantage is the central modern sense.
branches.cn: 决策线：对钱财与利益的去留迅速判断，是现代最核心的义项。

branches.en: THE EYE: the same sharpness applied to people and details rather than to a deal.
branches.cn: 眼睛线：同样的锋利用来看人和细节，而不是看交易。

branches.en: THE SHARP EDGE: calculating cleverness and pointed remarks both keep the old edge of the word.
branches.cn: 锋利线：算计的聪明与尖锐的话语，都保留了旧义的锋刃。

branches.en: The same judgement can look like business sense or like cunning, depending on who is being judged and by whom.
branches.cn: 同样的判断力，可以看作生意头脑，也可以看作狡猾，取决于被评判的对象与评判者。

branches.en: Sharp observation and a sharp question are the perception sense applied to the outside world.
branches.cn: 敏锐的观察与尖锐的提问，是把感知义用到外部世界。

intro.en: Shrewd is a short base adjective; English builds its family with -ly, -ness and -ish, and the old noun shrew behind it has no productive prefix.
intro.cn: shrewd 是短基础形容词；英语用 -ly、-ness、-ish 扩展出词族，而它背后的旧名词 shrew 并没有能产的词缀。

latinIntro.en: Shrewd has no Latin etymon: Old English screawa is the source of the animal name, and the word is native English, so no Latin relatives are listed.
latinIntro.cn: shrewd 没有拉丁语词源：古英语 screawa 是动物名的来源，这个词本身是英语本族词，因此不列拉丁同源词。

items.meaning: a small long-snouted mammal; an old insult for a scolding woman
items.meaningCN: 尖嘴小兽；旧时的贬称，指爱骂人的女人
items.example: The noun shrew is the base of the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 名词 shrew 是这个形容词的构词基础。

items.meaning: forming an adjective from a noun
items.meaningCN: 构成由名词派生的形容词
items.example: The adjective-ending -d in the older form of the word follows the pattern of words like bare and bald.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词词尾在这一词的旧形式中，遵循 bare、bald 一类词的构词路数。

items.example: Shrewd now carries no cruelty.
items.exampleCN: 现代 shrewd 已不再含残忍之意。

items.example: She judged the mood of the room shrewdly.
items.exampleCN: 她精明地判断出房间里的气氛。

items.example: The adverb ending -ly forms shrewdly from the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 副词词尾 -ly 把形容词构成 shrewdly。

items.example: His shrewdness saved the family business twice.
items.exampleCN: 他的精明两次救了家族生意。

items.meaningCN: 带有某种性质，程度较轻
items.example: The rare word shrewdish describes a mildly shrewd manner.
items.exampleCN: 罕见的 shrewdish 形容有点精明做派的样子。

items.example: Shrewish keeps the noun sense and has grown dated.
items.exampleCN: shrewish 保留了名词的旧义，如今已显过时。

definition_en: a small sea animal with a thin shell, long legs and a curved body, eaten as food; also an informal word for a small or unimportant person
core_image: 一只弯着腰的小虾，在水草间一弹一弹地倒退着游
scene: 渔港的清晨，摊位上摆着一网还在弹跳的小虾。The chef shelled the shrimp and dropped them into a pan of hot oil.
sceneCN: 这里 shrimp 是「虾」这种小型甲壳动物（第 1 个义项：可食用的虾）；句意：厨师把小虾去壳，丢进热油锅里。画面可想象：渔港摊位、竹篮、油锅。

pos.zh: 虾；小虾；小个子的活人（口语，略带贬义）
捕虾；极少用的动词义

collocations.zh: 明虾与小虾（英式英语常把大的叫 prawn）

derivatives.zh: 由本词加形容词后缀 -y 构成，义为「像虾一样的；矮小的」
由本词加名词后缀 -ing 构成，义为「捕虾；虾类捕捞业」
由 shrimp 与 boat 组成的复合词，义为「捕虾船」

senses.title: The small ten-legged shellfish
senses.definition: a small sea animal with a thin shell, a curved body and many pairs of legs, widely caught and eaten as food
senses.definitionCN: 体壳薄、身体弯曲、腿多，被广泛捕捞并作为食物的小型海生动物
senses.example: We bought a kilo of fresh shrimp at the market.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在市场买了一公斤新鲜小虾。
senses.why: The word goes back to a Germanic name for the animal, connected in etymology with the idea of shrivelling, curling up or shrinking; the small curled animal is the core image.
senses.whyCN: 这个词源自日耳曼语对这种动物的称呼，词源上与「皱缩、蜷曲、变小」的观念相关；那只小而蜷缩的动物就是核心意象。

senses.title: The food on a menu
senses.definition: shrimp used as an ingredient or dish, often with the flesh peeled and counted or sold by weight
senses.definitionCN: 作为食材或菜肴的虾，常去壳，或按只、按重量出售
senses.example: The starter was a bowl of shrimp with garlic butter.
senses.exampleCN: 开胃菜是一碗蒜香黄油虾。
senses.why: From the animal to the plate: once cooking turns the shellfish into food, the unchanged noun names the portion rather than the living creature.
senses.whyCN: 从动物到餐盘：一旦这甲壳类被做成食物，同一个名词指向的是那一份食材，而不是活着的生物。

senses.title: An informal word for a small person
senses.definition: an informal, mild and sometimes teasing name for someone short or unimportant, often said of a child
senses.definitionCN: 口语中略带戏谑地称呼个子矮或无关紧要的人，常用于孩子，语气较轻
senses.example: He was a shrimp of a boy until he suddenly grew tall at fifteen.
senses.exampleCN: 他十五岁突然长高之前，一直是个小豆丁。
senses.why: The animal is tiny and unimpressive, so the noun becomes a soft and mildly mocking label for a person who is small in body or in standing.
senses.whyCN: 这种动物个头小、不起眼，于是名词也成了对身材矮小或地位不高者的一种温和的戏称。

senses.title: To catch shrimp
senses.definition: to fish for or gather shrimp, mostly as a gerund in modern use
senses.definitionCN: 捕捞虾类，现代多用于动名词形式
senses.example: The boats go shrimping in the bay every autumn.
senses.exampleCN: 这些船每年秋天都到海湾里捕虾。
senses.why: The verb simply turns the animal into the activity: to name the catch is to name the trade of catching it.
senses.whyCN: 动词只是把动物名变成活动名：说出捕获物，就等于说出捕捞这门行当。

intro.en: Shrimp is an English and Germanic word for the small shellfish, and its deeper origin remains uncertain.
intro.cn: shrimp 是英语及日耳曼语中对这种小型甲壳类动物的称呼，更早的来源至今不确定。

items.en: A reconstructed form such as *skrimpan is usually proposed, but the exact shape is uncertain and no single reconstruction is agreed.
items.cn: 学界通常提出类似 *skrimpan 的重构形式，但确切形式不确定，也没有公认的单一构形。

items.en: Related forms in Scandinavian languages show the word had a wide Germanic range, so it is probably older than the English record.
items.cn: 斯堪的纳维亚各语言中的相关形式说明这个词在日耳曼语中分布很广，因此它很可能比英语的文献记录更古老。

items.en: Shrimpe names the small crustacean from the fourteenth century onward. The spelling varied a great deal in this period.
items.cn: 自十四世纪起 shrimpe 用来指这种小型甲壳动物。这一时期的拼写变化很多。

items.en: Many dictionaries relate the name to words meaning to shrivel, shrink or curl up; this is plausibly connected with the curved shape of the animal but is not certain.
items.cn: 不少词典把该名称与表示「皱缩、收缩、蜷曲」的词系联系起来；这可能与动物弯曲的体形有关，但并不确定。

items.en: The plural stays shrimp in American usage and is shrimps in most British usage. The fishing verb shrimping also appears in the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 复数在美式英语中常作 shrimp，英式英语中多用 shrimps。十九世纪还出现了表示「捕虾」的动名词 shrimping。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers shellfish names that are often confused in British and American usage; the near-meaning group gathers edible sea creatures of similar size and standing.
note.cn: 形近组收英美用法常混淆的甲壳动物名；近义组收个头与地位相近的可食用海味。

entries.definition: A large shrimp that is usually called a prawn in British shops; British cooks use prawn for the big ones and shrimp for the small ones.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指一种较大的虾；英国厨师通常把大的叫 prawn，小的叫 shrimp。与目标词是同一类动物的不同叫法。

entries.definition: A general word for sea animals with a shell, such as shrimp, crabs and lobsters; it is the class shrimp belongs to.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「有壳水产、甲壳与贝类」，是虾、蟹、龙虾等的统称，shrimp 正属于这一类。

entries.definition: A verb meaning to spend as little as possible; it looks close to shrimp but merely resembles it in spelling.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「节省、舍不得花钱」；只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: A small lobster-like creature that lives in fresh water and is also eaten.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「淡水螯虾」，形似小龙虾，生活在淡水，也可食用，与虾同属甲壳类。

entries.definition: A broad-shelled sea animal with big claws that walks sideways; a cousin of the shrimp in the same group.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「蟹」，壳宽、有螯、横着走，与虾同属甲壳动物。

entries.definition: A large sea shellfish with heavy claws, often a luxury dish; much bigger than a shrimp.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「龙虾」，有厚重的大螯，常作高档菜，个头比 shrimp 大得多。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Germanic history of the word and the phrases attached to the animal as food.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用这个词真实的日耳曼语源，以及它作为食物实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Shrimp is a native Germanic word, and the link with words for shrivelling fits the curled body.
normal.cn: shrimp 是日耳曼本族词，与表示「皱缩」的词系相连，正好对应蜷曲的身体。

normal.en: In British shops the big ones are prawns and the small ones are shrimps.
normal.cn: 在英国店铺里，大的叫 prawns，小的叫 shrimps。

normal.en: The American plural of shrimp is shrimp; the British one is usually shrimps.
normal.cn: shrimp 的复数在美式英语中是 shrimp，英式英语通常是 shrimps。

normal.en: Shrimp cocktail is a cold starter, and shrimp paste is a strong seasoning made from fermented shrimp.
normal.cn: shrimp cocktail 是冷盘开胃菜；shrimp paste 是用发酵虾制成的一种味道很冲的调味料。

normal.en: Compare prawn and lobster: a shrimp is the smallest of the three, both in size and in status.
normal.cn: 对比 prawn 与 lobster：无论在个头还是地位上，shrimp 都是三者中最小的。

abstract.en: Picture a pink shellfish flicking backwards through green water.
abstract.cn: 想象一只粉色的虾在绿水里向后一弹一弹地游。

abstract.en: Think of a plate of peeled shrimps curling in hot oil.
abstract.cn: 想象一碟去壳的虾在热油里蜷起来。

abstract.en: Imagine a small child standing on tiptoe to reach the counter.
abstract.cn: 想象一个小孩踮起脚尖去够柜台。

examples.en: The market sells shrimp by weight and prawns by handed count.
examples.cn: 这个市场里虾按重量卖，大虾按只数卖。

examples.en: My uncle shrimped along the coast for thirty years.
examples.cn: 我叔叔在海边捕虾捕了三十年。

examples.en: The boy was called a shrimp, but he was the fastest swimmer in class.
examples.cn: 这男孩被人叫做小豆丁，可他却是班里游得最快的人。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「虾润普」——虾肉湿润，普通人一顿能吃一小盘；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 英语 shrimp 来自日耳曼语系，一般认为与表示「皱缩、蜷曲」的词系相关，但更早形式不确定；它不是来自拉丁语，因此不列拉丁同源词。核心义「蜷着身体的小型甲壳动物」，并由此引申出「矮小的人」。

sensesIntro.en: Shrimp runs from the living animal, to the food on the plate, to a mild nickname for a small person, to the trade of catching it.
sensesIntro.cn: shrimp 由活着的动物，延伸到盘中的食物，再到对矮小者的温和戏称，最后到捕捉它的这门行当。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small curled shrimp flicking backwards through shallow water.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只蜷着身子的小虾，在浅水里向后弹游。

branches.en: THE ANIMAL: the physical shellfish with a thin shell and curved body is the root sense.
branches.cn: 动物线：壳薄、身弯的那只甲壳动物是词的本义。

branches.en: THE DISH: once cooked, the same word names the food and the portion.
branches.cn: 菜肴线：一旦被烹饪，同一个词就指食物和那一份分量。

branches.en: THE NICKNAME: small and unimpressive in the sea, the shrimp becomes a teasing name for a small person.
branches.cn: 戏称线：在海里个头小、不起眼，这个名于是成了对矮小者的戏称。

branches.en: THE WORK: the gerund shrimping turns the animal into a coastal trade.
branches.cn: 行当线：动名词 shrimping 把动物名变成了沿海的一种营生。

branches.en: Both senses rest on smallness: the physical size of the animal and the social size of the person.
branches.cn: 两个义项都建立在「小」上：动物的小是身体上的，人的小是地位上的。

intro.en: Shrimp is a simple Germanic base word with no prefix; English extends it with -y, -ing and compounds such as shrimpboat.
intro.cn: shrimp 是没有前缀的日耳曼基础词；英语用 -y、-ing 以及 shrimpboat 之类的复合词来扩展。

latinIntro.en: Shrimp has no Latin etymon; the animal is named in Germanic, and Latin shellfish words such as carabus are not related.
latinIntro.cn: shrimp 没有拉丁语词源；这种动物在日耳曼语中就已有名称，拉丁语中的 carabus 等甲壳类词跟它没有关系。

items.meaningCN: 可食用的小型甲壳动物
items.example: Shrimp is the unchanged base noun.
items.exampleCN: shrimp 是不变形的名词基础。

items.example: The ending -y gives shrimpy.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -y 构成 shrimpy。

items.example: Shrimpy can describe a thin, small build.
items.exampleCN: shrimpy 可以形容瘦小的体格。

items.example: The gerund ending -ing gives shrimping.
items.exampleCN: 动名词词尾 -ing 构成 shrimping。

items.meaning: a boat used for catching shrimp
items.example: Shrimpboat joins two nouns into one.
items.exampleCN: shrimpboat 把两个名词合为一个词。

items.meaning: a seasoning made from fermented shrimp
items.meaningCN: 用发酵虾制成的调味料
items.example: Shrimp paste gives soups a strong savoury taste.
items.exampleCN: 虾酱能给汤带来很浓的鲜味。

items.meaning: a cold dish of cooked shrimp with sauce
items.example: Shrimp cocktail is served cold with a sharp sauce.
items.exampleCN: 鲜虾杯是冷的，配一种酸辣的酱汁。

items.example: Prawn is the usual British word for the large ones.
items.exampleCN: prawn 是英式英语中称呼大虾的常用词。

definition_zh: 百叶窗；遮板；照相机快门；停止营业
definition_en: a hinged panel or wooden covering that closes over a window; the part of a camera that opens and closes to let in light; also to close a business for good
core_image: 一扇木页板在窗前一合，外面的光被整片挡住
scene: 午后老街，店主一点一点落下窗前的木页板，街上的光随之一寸寸退走。She pulled the shutters across the window before the storm reached the town.
sceneCN: 这里 shutter 是「窗板、百叶窗」（第 1 个义项：关合在窗外的遮板）；句意：风暴到达小镇前，她把窗板拉上。画面可想象：老街商铺、木窗框、一排竖条木页板。

pos.zh: 百叶窗；遮板；照相机快门；（剧院舞台的）防火幕
关上（窗板）；使（店铺）停业；用百叶窗遮住

derivatives.zh: 由本词加过去分词后缀 -ed 构成，义为「装有窗板的；停业的」
由本词加名词后缀 -ing 构成，在建筑领域义为「模板、模壳」，也指装窗板
由 shutter 与 bug 组成的复合词，口语中指「摄影迷」

senses.title: A hinged window panel
senses.definition: one of a pair of hinged panels, often of wood or louvred slats, fixed outside or inside a window to close it against light, sun or intrusion
senses.definitionCN: 一对铰接页板之一，常为木板或百叶条制成，装在窗外或窗内，用来遮挡光线、阳光或防范闯入
senses.example: The old cafe closed its wooden shutters at six.
senses.exampleCN: 那家老咖啡馆六点关上木窗板。
senses.why: The noun is formed from the verb shut, to close, with the agent suffix -er: a shutter is the thing that makes a window shut.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词由动词 shut（关闭）加表示「作用者」的后缀 -er 构成：shutter 就是让窗户关上的那件东西。

senses.title: The camera shutter
senses.definition: a mechanical device in a camera that opens for a measured time to let light reach the film or sensor
senses.definitionCN: 照相机中的机械装置，在设定的时间里打开，让光到达胶片或传感器
senses.example: A slow shutter made the passing cars into streaks of light.
senses.exampleCN: 较慢的快门把过往的汽车拍成了光带。
senses.why: The camera part uses the same image on a tiny scale: a curtain opens for an instant and closes again, just as a window shutter does.
senses.whyCN: 相机部件是把同一意象缩小到极小：帘幕瞬间打开又合上，和窗板开合的道理一样。

senses.title: The roll-down shutter of a shop
senses.titleCN: 卷帘门；商铺拉下的铁板
senses.definition: a rolling metal or wooden screen drawn down over a shopfront, often at night or when the business stops trading
senses.definitionCN: 拉在店面外的卷动金属或木质挡板，多在夜间或停业时拉下
senses.example: Shutters were down on half the shops along the street.
senses.exampleCN: 街上有一半店铺都拉下了卷帘门。
senses.why: A shop closed by a shutter is closed for the day or for good, so the object becomes the standard sign of a business that has stopped trading.
senses.whyCN: 拉下卷帘门的店铺意味着当天歇业或彻底停业，因此这件器物成了「生意关门」的标准标志。

senses.title: To close down for good
senses.definition: to close a business, office or public building permanently or for a long period
senses.definitionCN: 使企业、办公场所或公共建筑永久或长期关闭
senses.example: The factory shuttered its gates after forty years.
senses.exampleCN: 这家工厂在经营四十年后关上了大门。
senses.why: The verb turns the sign into the act: to shutter a place is to do to it what the shutter does to a window, close it and keep it closed.
senses.whyCN: 动词把标志变成动作：给某个地方上 shutter，就是让窗板对窗户所做之事，关上并且一直关着。

senses.title: The theatre safety curtain
senses.definition: a heavy fireproof curtain lowered between the stage and the audience in an emergency
senses.definitionCN: 剧院中在紧急情况下降落在舞台与观众之间的厚重防火帘幕
senses.example: At the sound of the alarm, the fire shutter came down.
senses.exampleCN: 警报一响，防火幕就落了下来。
senses.why: Here the shutter is not for light but for fire: a panel that closes the opening fast, which keeps the core image of a closing cover.
senses.whyCN: 这里的闸幕挡的不是光而是火：一块板迅速合上开口，仍保留「合盖」「关闭」的核心意象。

intro.en: Shutter is an English formation from the native verb shut plus the agent suffix -er, and shut itself is of uncertain older origin.
intro.cn: shutter 是英语本土构词：由本族动词 shut 加表示作用者的后缀 -er 组成；而 shut 本身更早的来源不确定。

items.en: Shut and its related forms record a practice of barring or fastening a door or a gate, and this sense of closing and keeping closed is the base.
items.cn: shut 及其相关形式记录的是插上闩、扣住门或栅的形象；「关闭并保持关闭」这一含义是基础。

items.en: The word is usually connected with shore and shoot and with an old sense of pushing or barring; the deeper origin and the oldest spelling are uncertain.
items.cn: 这个词通常与 shore、shoot 以及古时「推、闩」的含义相联系；更早的来源与最早的拼写都不确定。

items.en: Shutter appears as the noun for a closing cover, built from shut with the -er that also appears in cover and likewise names what does the closing.
items.cn: 十六世纪 shutter 作为「关闭的遮盖物」出现，由 shut 加 -er 构成，cover 中的 -er 同样指做关闭这个动作的东西。

items.en: Photography adopted the word for the timing mechanism of the lens from the 1840s, and shops adopted roll-down shutters for their fronts.
items.cn: 摄影自十九世纪四十年代起用这个词指镜头上的控时装置；店铺也开始在正门使用卷动铁板。

items.en: The verb to shutter extends the object into action: to close a window with shutters, and nowadays to close a business for good.
items.cn: 动词 to shutter 把器物延伸到动作：用窗板关上窗户，如今也指让一家企业永久停业。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the verb shut and the -er family built on it; the near-meaning group gathers window and door coverings and the camera part with a similar closing action.
note.cn: 形近组收动词 shut 以及由它加 -er 构成的词族；近义组收窗门遮盖物以及开合动作相近的相机部件。

entries.definition: To close something, or to become closed, often firmly or for a long time.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「关闭；关上」，常指紧紧地关上或长久关上，是 shutter 的构词基础。

entries.definition: The plural noun, also used in idioms such as pulling the shutters down on a failed business.
entries.definitionCN: 名词复数形式，也用于习语：给失败的企业「拉下闸门」，即停业收场。

entries.definition: The act of firing, filming or taking photographs; it starts with the same letters as shutter but merely looks similar.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「射击、拍摄」，与 shutter 开头字母相同，只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: A window covering of slats or fabric that can be drawn up or down; softer and more flexible than a shutter.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「百叶帘、窗帘」，由片条或布料制成，可上下拉动，比 shutter 柔软灵活。

entries.definition: A piece of hanging cloth pulled across a window or a stage; cloth rather than a rigid panel.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「窗帘、幕布」，是挂在窗前或舞台前的布，而非硬板。

entries.definition: The adjustable opening in a camera lens that controls light; the shutter opens and closes in front of it.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「光圈、孔径」，指镜头中可调节的开口，控制进光量；快门在它的前方开合。属摄影术语。

normalIntro.en: These hooks rest on the real structure of the word, a native verb plus -er, and on the phrases it actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子依据这个词的真实结构，即本族动词加 -er，以及它实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Shutter is shut plus -er: the thing that shuts a window.
normal.cn: shutter 是 shut 加 -er：让窗户关上的那件东西。

normal.en: The -er ending appears in cover, a thing that covers; a shutter is what shuts.
normal.cn: cover 中的 -er 表示遮盖之物；shutter 就是「关闭之物」。

normal.en: Pull down the shutters means the shop has closed, and put them up means it is open for business again.
normal.cn: pull down the shutters 表示店铺已歇业；put them up 表示重新开门做生意。

normal.en: Shutter speed decides how long the camera lets light in.
normal.cn: shutter speed（快门速度）决定相机让光进来多久。

normal.en: Compare blind: a blind is cloth or slats, a shutter is a solid panel that closes.
normal.cn: 对比 blind：blind 是布或片条，shutter 是合拢的硬板。

abstract.en: Picture a wooden panel swinging shut over a lit window.
abstract.cn: 想象一块木页板摆动着合上，挡住亮着的窗户。

abstract.en: Think of a metal roller rumbling down over a shopfront at night.
abstract.cn: 想象夜里一块金属卷板咔嗒咔嗒落到店面前。

abstract.en: Imagine a camera clicking once, so that the light has only one instant to arrive.
abstract.cn: 想象相机「咔」地响一声，光只有一瞬间能进来。

examples.en: She latched the shutters before the wind grew stronger.
examples.cn: 风变大之前，她把窗板扣好。

examples.en: A high shutter speed freezes a bird in mid-flight.
examples.cn: 高快门速度能把飞鸟定格在半空中。

examples.en: The old printing house shuttered its doors last spring.
examples.cn: 那家老印刷厂去年春天关门停业了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「沙特」——沙子特多地刮来时，家家赶紧合上窗板；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 英语本土构成：shut（关闭，源自古英语，更早来源不确定）加后缀 -er（做某事者或所用之物）→ shutter（关合之物）。同族可见 shut、shutter、shuttered；与拉丁语无直接同源关系。

sensesIntro.en: Shutter starts from the thing that shuts a window, then covers the camera part, the shopfront panel, the act of closing a business for good, and the theatre fire curtain.
sensesIntro.cn: shutter 从「关上窗户的那件东西」出发，再扩展到相机上的部件、门面的卷板、让生意永久停业的动作，以及剧院的防火幕。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a panel swings shut across an opening, and the light on the other side disappears.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块板合上来盖住开口，另一侧的光随之消失。

branches.en: THE WINDOW: a hinged panel closing over glass is the original everyday sense.
branches.cn: 窗户线：合在玻璃外的铰接页板，是原本的日常义项。

branches.en: THE LIGHT AND THE FIRE: one device stops light on a camera and another stops fire in a theatre, both by closing fast.
branches.cn: 光与火线：一个器械在相机上挡光，另一个在剧院里挡火，做法都是迅速合上。

branches.en: THE SHOPFRONT: a roll-down screen makes the shutter the visible sign of a closed shop.
branches.cn: 店面线：卷动挡板让 shutter 成为店铺关门最直观的标志。

branches.en: THE ACT: the verb turns the object into the act of closing a business for good.
branches.cn: 动作线：动词把器物变成「永久关门」这个动作。

branches.en: The link runs from a board over a window to a board over a shopfront, and finally to the end of the trade behind it.
branches.cn: 脉络从窗前的板，到门前的板，最后到板后那门生意的终结。

intro.en: Shutter is a native English formation, a verb plus the agent suffix -er; its English family grows with -ed, -ing and compounds.
intro.cn: shutter 是英语本族构词，由动词加表示作用者的后缀 -er 组成；英语词族再以 -ed、-ing 与复合词扩展。

latinIntro.en: Neither shutter nor the verb shut has a Latin etymon, so no Latin relatives are listed here.
latinIntro.cn: shutter 与动词 shut 都没有拉丁语词源，因此这里不列拉丁同源词。

items.example: The noun comes from the verb shut.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词来自动词 shut。

items.meaning: the person or thing that does
items.example: The agent ending -er turns shut into the name of the closing thing.
items.exampleCN: 作用者词尾 -er 把 shut 变成「关合之物」的名称。

items.meaning: a closing panel for a window; a camera part
items.meaningCN: 窗户上的关合板；相机部件
items.example: Shutter is both the noun and, nowadays, the verb.
items.exampleCN: shutter 既是名词，如今也用作动词。

items.meaning: the pair of panels on a window
items.example: Shutters are usually fitted in pairs.
items.exampleCN: 窗板通常是成对安装的。

items.example: The past-participle ending -ed forms shuttered.
items.exampleCN: 过去分词后缀 -ed 构成 shuttered。

items.example: Shuttered houses stood along the quiet street.
items.exampleCN: 安静的老街上，一栋栋房子都关着窗板。

items.example: The noun ending -ing forms shuttering, a builder term for formwork.
items.exampleCN: 名词后缀 -ing 构成 shuttering，是建筑行业的「模板、模壳」术语。

items.example: Shutterbug joins shutter and bug in casual use.
items.exampleCN: shutterbug 在口语中把 shutter 与 bug 合成一词。

items.meaning: how long the camera shutter stays open
items.example: Shutter speed is measured in fractions of a second.
items.exampleCN: 快门速度以几分之一秒为单位计量。
